75.s:
rudra uvāca .
ata ūrdhvaṃ pravakṣyāmi jambūdvīpaṃ yathātatham .
saṃkhyāṃ cāpi samudrāṇāṃ dvīpānāṃ caiva vistaram .. 75.1 ..
75.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं प्रवक्ष्यामि जम्बूद्वीपं यथातथम् ।
संख्यां चापि समुद्राणां द्वीपानां चैव विस्तरम् ॥ 75.1 ॥
75.m:
Thus ends the seventy-fourth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, the venerable scripture.

Rudra said: / Hereafter I shall explain Jambūdvīpa as it truly is, / and the number of the oceans, and the extent of the continents,

75.s:
yāvanti caiva varṣāṇi teṣu nadyaśca yāḥ smṛtāḥ .
mahābhūtapramāṇaṃ ca gatiṃ candrārkayoḥ pṛthak .. 75.2 ..
75.d:
यावन्ति चैव वर्षाणि तेषु नद्यश्च याः स्मृताः ।
महाभूतप्रमाणं च गतिं चन्द्रार्कयोः पृथक् ॥ 75.2 ॥
75.m: and as many realms as there are, the rivers recorded in them, / the measure of the great elements, and the individual motion of the moon and the sun.

75.s:
dvīpabhedasahastrāṇi saptasvantargatāni ca .
na śakyante krameṇeha vaktuṃ yairvitataṃ jagat .. 75.3 ..
75.d:
द्वीपभेदसहस्त्राणि सप्तस्वन्तर्गतानि च ।
न शक्यन्ते क्रमेणेह वक्तुं यैर्विततं जगत् ॥ 75.3 ॥
75.m: The thousands of continental divisions situated within the seven, / by which the world is covered, cannot be described here in sequence.

75.s:
saptadvīpān pravakṣyāmi candrādityagrahaiḥ saha .
yeṣāṃ manuṣyāstarkeṇa pramāṇāni pracakṣate .. 75.4 ..
75.d:
सप्तद्वीपान् प्रवक्ष्यामि चन्द्रादित्यग्रहैः सह ।
येषां मनुष्यास्तर्केण प्रमाणानि प्रचक्षते ॥ 75.4 ॥
75.m: I shall describe the seven continents, together with the moon, sun, and planets, / whose dimensions humans proclaim by means of inference.

75.s:
acintyāḥ khalu ye bhāvā na tāṃstarkeṇa sādhayet .
prakṛtibhyaḥ paraṃ yacca tadacintyaṃ vibhāvyate .. 75.5 ..
75.d:
अचिन्त्याः खलु ये भावा न तांस्तर्केण साधयेत् ।
प्रकृतिभ्यः परं यच्च तदचिन्त्यं विभाव्यते ॥ 75.5 ॥
75.m: States of being that are beyond thought one should indeed not establish by inference; / that which is beyond the primary material constituents is considered inconceivable.

75.s:
nava varṣaṃ pravakṣyāmi jambūdvīpaṃ yathātatham .
vistarānmaṇḍalāccaiva yojanaistannibodhata .. 75.6 ..
75.d:
नव वर्षं प्रवक्ष्यामि जम्बूद्वीपं यथातथम् ।
विस्तरान्मण्डलाच्चैव योजनैस्तन्निबोधत ॥ 75.6 ॥
75.m: I shall describe Jambūdvīpa, which has nine realms, as it truly is, / in its breadth and circumference, in yojanas; listen to it:

75.s:
śatamekaṃ sahastrāṇāṃ yojanānāṃ samantataḥ .
nānājanapadākīrṇaṃ yojanairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 75.7 ..
75.d:
शतमेकं सहस्त्राणां योजनानां समन्ततः ।
नानाजनपदाकीर्णं योजनैर्विविधैः शुभैः ॥ 75.7 ॥
75.m: It is one hundred thousand yojanas in every direction, / filled with various provinces, with many auspicious yojanas,

75.s:
siddhacāraṇasaṃkīrṇaṃ parvatairupaśobhitam .
sarvadhātuvivṛddhaiśca śilājālasamudbhavaiḥ .
parvataprabhavābhiśca nadībhiḥ sarvataścitam .. 75.8 ..
75.d:
सिद्धचारणसंकीर्णं पर्वतैरुपशोभितम् ।
सर्वधातुविवृद्धैश्च शिलाजालसमुद्भवैः ।
पर्वतप्रभवाभिश्च नदीभिः सर्वतश्चितम् ॥ 75.8 ॥
75.m: crowded with Siddhas and Cāraṇas, adorned with mountains, / rich in all minerals, arising from masses of rocks, / and covered on all sides with rivers originating from the mountains.

75.s:
jambūdvīpaḥ pṛthuḥ śrīmān sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaḥ .
navabhiścāvṛtaḥ śrīmān bhuvanairbhūtabhāvanaḥ .. 75.9 ..
75.d:
जम्बूद्वीपः पृथुः श्रीमान् सर्वतः परिमण्डलः ।
नवभिश्चावृतः श्रीमान् भुवनैर्भूतभावनः ॥ 75.9 ॥
75.m: Jambūdvīpa is broad, glorious, circular on all sides, / glorious, encompassing nine worlds, bringing forth living beings,

75.s:
lavaṇena samudreṇa sarvataḥ parivāritaḥ .
jambūdvīpasya vistārāt samena tu samantataḥ .. 75.10 ..
75.d:
लवणेन समुद्रेण सर्वतः परिवारितः ।
जम्बूद्वीपस्य विस्तारात् समेन तु समन्ततः ॥ 75.10 ॥
75.m: surrounded on all sides by the ocean of salt water, / which is equal in extent all around to the breadth of Jambūdvīpa.

75.s:
tasya prāgāyatā dīrghā ṣaḍete varṣaparvatāḥ .
ubhayatrāvagāḍhāśca samudrau pūrvapaścimau .. 75.11 ..
75.d:
तस्य प्रागायता दीर्घा षडेते वर्षपर्वताः ।
उभयत्रावगाढाश्च समुद्रौ पूर्वपश्चिमौ ॥ 75.11 ॥
75.m: Its six realm-mountains are long, stretching to the east, / and immersed on both sides into the eastern and western oceans:

75.s:
himaprāyaśca himavān hemakūṭaśca hemavān .
sarvatra susukhaścāpi niṣadhaḥ parvato mahān .. 75.12 ..
75.d:
हिमप्रायश्च हिमवान् हेमकूटश्च हेमवान् ।
सर्वत्र सुसुखश्चापि निषधः पर्वतो महान् ॥ 75.12 ॥
75.m: Himavant, abounding in snow; Hemakūṭa, abounding in gold; / and the great mountain Niṣadha, entirely pleasant everywhere.

75.s:
caturvarṇaḥsa sauvarṇo meruścolbamayo giriḥ .
vṛttākṛtipramāṇaśca caturastraḥ samucchitaḥ .. 75.13 ..
75.d:
चतुर्वर्णःस सौवर्णो मेरुश्चोल्बमयो गिरिः ।
वृत्ताकृतिप्रमाणश्च चतुरस्त्रः समुच्छितः ॥ 75.13 ॥
75.m: Mount Meru is four-colored, golden, and immense, / having a circular shape and dimension, [yet] four-cornered and lofty,

75.s:
nānāvarṇastu pārśveṣu prajāpatiguṇānvitaḥ .
nābhimaṇḍalasaṃbhūto brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ .. 75.14 ..
75.d:
नानावर्णस्तु पार्श्वेषु प्रजापतिगुणान्वितः ।
नाभिमण्डलसंभूतो ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः ॥ 75.14 ॥
75.m: of various colors on its sides, endowed with the qualities of Prajāpati, / born from the circular navel of Brahmā, the supreme lord.

75.s:
pūrvataḥ śvetavarṇastu brahmaṇyaṃ tena tasya tat .
pītaśca dakṣiṇenāsau tena vaiśyatvamiṣyate .. 75.15 ..
75.d:
पूर्वतः श्वेतवर्णस्तु ब्रह्मण्यं तेन तस्य तत् ।
पीतश्च दक्षिणेनासौ तेन वैश्यत्वमिष्यते ॥ 75.15 ॥
75.m: On the east it is white in color, and therefore belongs to the brāhmaṇa class; / and it is yellow on the south, wherefore it is considered to belong to the vaiśya class.

75.s:
bhṛṅgapatranibhaścāsau paścimena yato'tha saḥ .
tenāsya śūdratā proktā merornāmārthakarmaṇaḥ .. 75.16 ..
75.d:
भृङ्गपत्रनिभश्चासौ पश्चिमेन यतोऽथ सः ।
तेनास्य शूद्रता प्रोक्ता मेरोर्नामार्थकर्मणः ॥ 75.16 ॥
75.m: And since it resembles a black bee’s wing on the west, / its śūdra nature is proclaimed, of Meru whose actions correspond to the meaning of its names.

75.s:
pārśvamuttaratastasya raktavarṇaṃ vibhāvyate.
tenāsya kṣatrabhāvaḥ syāditi varṇāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 75.17 ..
75.d:
पार्श्वमुत्तरतस्तस्य रक्तवर्णं विभाव्यते।
तेनास्य क्षत्रभावः स्यादिति वर्णाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 75.17 ॥
75.m: Its northern flank is perceived to be red in color; / by this it has the nature of a kṣatriya: thus the castes have been proclaimed.

75.s:
vṛttaḥ svabhāvataḥ prokto varṇataḥ parimāṇataḥ .
nīlaśca vaidūryamayaḥ śvetaśuklo hiraṇmayaḥ .
mayūrabarhivarṇastu śātakaumbhaśca śrṛṅgavān .. 75.18 ..
75.d:
वृत्तः स्वभावतः प्रोक्तो वर्णतः परिमाणतः ।
नीलश्च वैदूर्यमयः श्वेतशुक्लो हिरण्मयः ।
मयूरबर्हिवर्णस्तु शातकौम्भश्च श्रृङ्गवान् ॥ 75.18 ॥
75.m: It is declared to be round by nature, by color, and by measurement. / And Nīla is made of lapis lazuli; Śveta is white and golden; / while Śṛṅgavān is colored like a peacock’s tail-feather and made of gold.

75.s:
ete parvatarājānaḥ siddhacāraṇasevitāḥ .
teṣāmantaraviṣkambho navasāhastra ucyate .. 75.19 ..
75.d:
एते पर्वतराजानः सिद्धचारणसेविताः ।
तेषामन्तरविष्कम्भो नवसाहस्त्र उच्यते ॥ 75.19 ॥
75.m: These are the kingly mountains, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas; / the intervening extent between them is said to be nine thousand [yojanas].

75.s:
madhye tvilāvṛtaṃ nāma mahāmeroḥ sa saṃbhavaḥ .
navaiva tu sahastrāṇi vistīrṇaḥ sarvataśca saḥ .. 75.20 ..
75.d:
मध्ये त्विलावृतं नाम महामेरोः स संभवः ।
नवैव तु सहस्त्राणि विस्तीर्णः सर्वतश्च सः ॥ 75.20 ॥
75.m: In the center is Ilāvṛta, the domain of Mahāmeru; / and it extends for nine thousand [yojanas] on every side.

75.s:
madhyaṃ tasya mahāmerurvidhūma iva pāvakaḥ .
vedyarddhaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ meroruttarārddhaṃ tathottaram .. 75.21 ..
75.d:
मध्यं तस्य महामेरुर्विधूम इव पावकः ।
वेद्यर्द्धं दक्षिणं मेरोरुत्तरार्द्धं तथोत्तरम् ॥ 75.21 ॥
75.m: Mahāmeru stands in its center like a smokeless fire; / half the altar is to the south of Meru, and half the altar is likewise to the north.

75.s:
varṣāṇi yāni ṣaḍatra teṣāṃ te varṣaparvatāḥ .
yojanāgraṃ tu varṣāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ tad vidhīyate .. 75.22 ..
75.d:
वर्षाणि यानि षडत्र तेषां ते वर्षपर्वताः ।
योजनाग्रं तु वर्षाणां सर्वेषां तद् विधीयते ॥ 75.22 ॥
75.m: The six realms (varṣas) that are here have those realm-mountains (varṣaparvatas); / that peak-measurement in yojanas is prescribed for all the varṣas.

75.s:
dve dve varṣe sahastrāṇāṃ yojanānāṃ samucchrayaḥ .
jambūdvīpasya vistārasteṣāmāyāma ucyate .. 75.23 ..
75.d:
द्वे द्वे वर्षे सहस्त्राणां योजनानां समुच्छ्रयः ।
जम्बूद्वीपस्य विस्तारस्तेषामायाम उच्यते ॥ 75.23 ॥
75.m: Two thousand yojanas is the height in each realm; / the breadth of Jambūdvīpa is declared to be their length.

75.s:
yojanānāṃ sahastrāṇi śatau dvau cāyatau girī .
nīlaśca niṣadhaścaiva tābhyāṃ hīnāśca ye pare .
śvetaśca hemakūṭaśca himavāñchṛṅgavāṃśca yaḥ .. 75.24 ..
75.d:
योजनानां सहस्त्राणि शतौ द्वौ चायतौ गिरी ।
नीलश्च निषधश्चैव ताभ्यां हीनाश्च ये परे ।
श्वेतश्च हेमकूटश्च हिमवाञ्छृङ्गवांश्च यः ॥ 75.24 ॥
75.m: Two mountains extend for two hundred thousand yojanas: / Nīla and Niṣadha; and those that follow are lesser than them: / Śveta, Hemakūṭa, Himavān, and Śṛṅgavān.

75.s:
jambūdvīpapramāṇena niṣadhaḥ parikīrtitaḥ .
tasmād dvādaśabhāgena hemakūṭaḥ prahīyate .
himavān viṃśabhāgena hemakūṭāt prahīyate .. 75.25 ..
75.d:
जम्बूद्वीपप्रमाणेन निषधः परिकीर्तितः ।
तस्माद् द्वादशभागेन हेमकूटः प्रहीयते ।
हिमवान् विंशभागेन हेमकूटात् प्रहीयते ॥ 75.25 ॥
75.m: Niṣadha is proclaimed to be of the extent of Jambūdvīpa; / Hemakūṭa is less than that by a twelfth part; / Himavān is less than Hemakūṭa by a twentieth part.

75.s:
aṣṭāśītisahastrāṇi hemakūṭo mahāgiriḥ .
aśītirhimavān śaila āyataḥ pūrvapaścime .. 75.26 ..
75.d:
अष्टाशीतिसहस्त्राणि हेमकूटो महागिरिः ।
अशीतिर्हिमवान् शैल आयतः पूर्वपश्चिमे ॥ 75.26 ॥
75.m: Hemakūṭa, the great mountain, is eighty-eight thousand [yojanas]; / Mount Himavān is eighty thousand, extending east and west.

75.s:
dvīpasya maṇḍalībhāvād hrāsavṛddhī prakīrtyate .
varṣāṇāṃ parvatānāṃ ca yathā ceme tathottaram .. 75.27 ..
75.d:
द्वीपस्य मण्डलीभावाद् ह्रासवृद्धी प्रकीर्त्यते ।
वर्षाणां पर्वतानां च यथा चेमे तथोत्तरम् ॥ 75.27 ॥
75.m: Decrease and increase are proclaimed on account of the circular nature of the continent, / for both the varṣas and the mountains, just as these [are situated] toward the north.

75.s:
teṣāṃ madhye janapadāstāni varṣāṇi caiva tat .
prapātaviṣamaistaistu parvatairāvṛtāni tu .. 75.28 ..
75.d:
तेषां मध्ये जनपदास्तानि वर्षाणि चैव तत् ।
प्रपातविषमैस्तैस्तु पर्वतैरावृतानि तु ॥ 75.28 ॥
75.m: In their midst are inhabited countries and those very realms, / which are enclosed by various mountains impassable with precipices,

75.s:
saṃtatāni nadībhedairagamyāni parasparam .
vasanti teṣu sattvāni nānājātīni sarvaśaḥ .. 75.29 ..
75.d:
संततानि नदीभेदैरगम्यानि परस्परम् ।
वसन्ति तेषु सत्त्वानि नानाजातीनि सर्वशः ॥ 75.29 ॥
75.m: traversed by various rivers and mutually inaccessible; / living creatures of manifold species dwell upon them everywhere.

75.s:
etaddhaimavataṃ varṣaṃ bhāratī yatra santatiḥ .
hemakūṭaṃ paraṃ yatra nāmnā kiṃpuruṣottamaḥ .. 75.30 ..
75.d:
एतद्धैमवतं वर्षं भारती यत्र सन्ततिः ।
हेमकूटं परं यत्र नाम्ना किंपुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 75.30 ॥
75.m: This is the Haimavata realm, where the descendants of Bharata dwell; / beyond it is Hemakūṭa, where the realm named Kiṃpuruṣottama lies.

75.s:
hemakūṭāt tu niṣadhaṃ harivarṣaṃ taducyate .
harivarṣāt paraṃ caiva merupārśva ilāvṛtam .. 75.31 ..
75.d:
हेमकूटात् तु निषधं हरिवर्षं तदुच्यते ।
हरिवर्षात् परं चैव मेरुपार्श्व इलावृतम् ॥ 75.31 ॥
75.m: Beyond Hemakūṭa lies Niṣadha, and that is called Harivarṣa; / and beyond Harivarṣa, on the flank of Meru, is Ilāvṛta.

75.s:
ilāvṛtāt paraṃ nīlaṃ ramyakaṃ nāma viśrutam .
ramyakācca paraṃ śvetaṃ viśrutaṃ taddhiraṇmayam .
hiraṇmayāt paraṃ caiva śrṛṅgavantaṃ kuru smṛtam .. 75.32 ..
75.d:
इलावृतात् परं नीलं रम्यकं नाम विश्रुतम् ।
रम्यकाच्च परं श्वेतं विश्रुतं तद्धिरण्मयम् ।
हिरण्मयात् परं चैव श्रृङ्गवन्तं कुरु स्मृतम् ॥ 75.32 ॥
75.m: Beyond Ilāvṛta is Nīla, renowned by the name Ramyaka; / beyond Ramyaka is Śveta, celebrated as Hiraṇmaya; / and beyond Hiraṇmaya, at Mount Śṛṅgavān, Kuru is recorded.

75.s:
dhanuḥsaṃsthe tu dve varṣe vijñeye dakṣiṇottare .
dvīpāni khalu catvāri caturastramilāvṛtam .. 75.33 ..
75.d:
धनुःसंस्थे तु द्वे वर्षे विज्ञेये दक्षिणोत्तरे ।
द्वीपानि खलु चत्वारि चतुरस्त्रमिलावृतम् ॥ 75.33 ॥
75.m: The two realms situated to the south and the north should be known as bow-shaped; / there are indeed four continents, and Ilāvṛta is quadrangular.

75.s:
arvāk ca niṣadhasyātha vedyardhaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ smṛtam .
paraṃ śrṛṅgavato yacca vedyardhaṃ hi taduttaram .. 75.34 ..
75.d:
अर्वाक् च निषधस्याथ वेद्यर्धं दक्षिणं स्मृतम् ।
परं श्रृङ्गवतो यच्च वेद्यर्धं हि तदुत्तरम् ॥ 75.34 ॥
75.m: Hither from Niṣadha, half of the altar is recorded as southern; / and that which is beyond Śṛṅgavān is indeed the northern half of the altar.

75.s:
vedyarddhe dakṣiṇe trīṇi varṣāṇi trīṇi cottare .
tayormadhye tu vijñeyo yatra merustvilāvṛtaḥ .. 75.35 ..
75.d:
वेद्यर्द्धे दक्षिणे त्रीणि वर्षाणि त्रीणि चोत्तरे ।
तयोर्मध्ये तु विज्ञेयो यत्र मेरुस्त्विलावृतः ॥ 75.35 ॥
75.m: There are three realms in the southern half of the altar, and three in the northern; / and between the two should be known [the realm] where Meru stands, namely Ilāvṛta.

75.s:
dakṣiṇena tu nīlasya niṣadhasyottareṇa ca .
udagāyato mahāśailo mālyavānnāma parvataḥ .. 75.36 ..
75.d:
दक्षिणेन तु नीलस्य निषधस्योत्तरेण च ।
उदगायतो महाशैलो माल्यवान्नाम पर्वतः ॥ 75.36 ॥
75.m: To the south of Nīla and to the north of Niṣadha / lies the great mountain named Mālyavān, extending northward.

75.s:
yojanānāṃ sahastre dve viṣkambhocchraya eva ca .
āyāmataścatustriṃśat sahastrāṇi prakīrtitaḥ .. 75.37 ..
75.d:
योजनानां सहस्त्रे द्वे विष्कम्भोच्छ्रय एव च ।
आयामतश्चतुस्त्रिंशत् सहस्त्राणि प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 75.37 ॥
75.m: It is two thousand yojanas in both breadth and height; / in length it is proclaimed to be thirty-four thousand.

75.s:
tasya pratīcyāṃ vijñeyaḥ parvato gandhamādanaḥ .
āyāmocchrayavistārāt tulyo mālyavatā tu saḥ .. 75.38 ..
75.d:
तस्य प्रतीच्यां विज्ञेयः पर्वतो गन्धमादनः ।
आयामोच्छ्रयविस्तारात् तुल्यो माल्यवता तु सः ॥ 75.38 ॥
75.m: To its west is to be known Mount Gandhamādana; / in length, height, and breadth it is equal to Mālyavān.

75.s:
parimaṇḍalastayormadhye meruḥ kanakaparvataḥ .
caturvarṇaḥ sasauvarṇaścaturastraḥ samucchritaḥ .. 75.39 ..
75.d:
परिमण्डलस्तयोर्मध्ये मेरुः कनकपर्वतः ।
चतुर्वर्णः ससौवर्णश्चतुरस्त्रः समुच्छ्रितः ॥ 75.39 ॥
75.m: Between them is circular Meru, the golden mountain, / endowed with four colors, golden, four-cornered, and elevated.

75.s:
avyaktā dhātavaḥ sarve samutpannā jalādayaḥ .
avyaktāt pṛthivīpadmaṃ merustasya ca karṇikā .. 75.40 ..
75.d:
अव्यक्ता धातवः सर्वे समुत्पन्ना जलादयः ।
अव्यक्तात् पृथिवीपद्मं मेरुस्तस्य च कर्णिका ॥ 75.40 ॥
75.m: All the elements, water and the rest, arose from the unmanifest; / from the unmanifest came the Earth-lotus, and Meru is its pericarp.

75.s:
catuṣpatraṃ samutpannaṃ vyaktaṃ pañcaguṇaṃ mahat .
tataḥ sarvāḥ samudbhūtā vitatā hi pravṛttayaḥ .. 75.41 ..
75.d:
चतुष्पत्रं समुत्पन्नं व्यक्तं पञ्चगुणं महत् ।
ततः सर्वाः समुद्भूता वितता हि प्रवृत्तयः ॥ 75.41 ॥
75.m: The great manifest world of five qualities arose with four petals; / from that were produced all the widespread activities [of creation].

75.s:
anekakalpajīvadbhiḥ puruṣaiḥ puṇyakāribhiḥ .
kṛtātmabhirmahātmabhiḥ prāpyate puruṣottamaḥ .. 75.42 ..
75.d:
अनेककल्पजीवद्भिः पुरुषैः पुण्यकारिभिः ।
कृतात्मभिर्महात्मभिः प्राप्यते पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 75.42 ॥
75.m: By men who live through many kalpas, who perform meritorious deeds, / who have purified their selves and are great-souled, the Supreme Person is attained.

75.s:
mahāyogī mahādevo jagaddhyeyo janārdanaḥ .
sarvalokagato'nanto vyāpako mūrttiravyayaḥ .. 75.43 ..
75.d:
महायोगी महादेवो जगद्ध्येयो जनार्दनः ।
सर्वलोकगतोऽनन्तो व्यापको मूर्त्तिरव्ययः ॥ 75.43 ॥
75.m: Janārdana is the great yogin, the great deity, the object of meditation for the world, / present in all worlds, infinite, all-pervading, having form, immutable.

75.s:
na tasya prākṛtā mūrtirmāṃsamedo'sthisaṃbhavā .
yogitvācceśvaratvācca sattvarūpadharo vibhuḥ .. 75.44 ..
75.d:
न तस्य प्राकृता मूर्तिर्मांसमेदोऽस्थिसंभवा ।
योगित्वाच्चेश्वरत्वाच्च सत्त्वरूपधरो विभुः ॥ 75.44 ॥
75.m: His form is not material, born of flesh, fat, and bone; / through His nature as yogin and His sovereignty, the Lord assumes the form of sattva.

75.s:
tannimittaṃ samutpannaṃ loke padmaṃ sanātanam .
kalpaśeṣasya tasyādau kālasya gatirīdṛśī .. 75.45 ..
75.d:
तन्निमित्तं समुत्पन्नं लोके पद्मं सनातनम् ।
कल्पशेषस्य तस्यादौ कालस्य गतिरीदृशी ॥ 75.45 ॥
75.m: For His purpose the eternal lotus arose in the world; / at the beginning of the remainder of that kalpa, such is the course of time.

75.s:
tasmin padme samutpanno devadevaścaturmukhaḥ .
prajāpatipatirdeva īśāno jagataḥ prabhuḥ .. 75.46 ..
75.d:
तस्मिन् पद्मे समुत्पन्नो देवदेवश्चतुर्मुखः ।
प्रजापतिपतिर्देव ईशानो जगतः प्रभुः ॥ 75.46 ॥
75.m: Upon that lotus was born the four-faced god of gods, / the lord of the lords of creatures, the god, the sovereign, the ruler of the world.

75.s:
tasya bījanisargaṃ hi puṣkarasya yathārthavat .
kṛtsnaṃ prajānisargeṇa vistareṇaiva varṇyate .. 75.47 ..
75.d:
तस्य बीजनिसर्गं हि पुष्करस्य यथार्थवत् ।
कृत्स्नं प्रजानिसर्गेण विस्तरेणैव वर्ण्यते ॥ 75.47 ॥
75.m: The distribution of seeds for that lotus, according to reality, / is described in its entirety and in detail through the emission of creatures.

75.s:
tadambu vaiṣṇavaḥ kāyo yato ratnavibhūṣitaḥ .
padmākārā samutpannā pṛthivī savanadrumā .. 75.48 ..
75.d:
तदम्बु वैष्णवः कायो यतो रत्नविभूषितः ।
पद्माकारा समुत्पन्ना पृथिवी सवनद्रुमा ॥ 75.48 ॥
75.m: That water is the body of Viṣṇu, since it is adorned with jewels; / the Earth, with forests and trees, arose in the form of a lotus.

75.s:
tat tasya lokapadmasya vistaraṃ siddhabhāṣitam .
varṇyamānaṃ vibhāgena kramaśaḥ śrṛṇuta dvijāḥ .. 75.49 ..
75.d:
तत् तस्य लोकपद्मस्य विस्तरं सिद्धभाषितम् ।
वर्ण्यमानं विभागेन क्रमशः श्रृणुत द्विजाः ॥ 75.49 ॥
75.m: Listen, O twice-born, in succession to the extent of that world-lotus / as spoken by the Siddhas, being described part by part.

75.s:
mahāvarṣāṇi khyātāni catvāryatra ca saṃsthitāḥ .
tatra parvatasaṃsthāno merurnāma mahābalaḥ .. 75.50 ..
75.d:
महावर्षाणि ख्यातानि चत्वार्यत्र च संस्थिताः ।
तत्र पर्वतसंस्थानो मेरुर्नाम महाबलः ॥ 75.50 ॥
75.m: Four great realms are celebrated as situated here; / there stands the mountain-mass named Meru of great might.

75.s:
nānāvarṇaḥ sa pārśveṣu pūrvataḥ śveta ucyate .
pītaṃ ca dakṣiṇaṃ tasya bhṛṅgavarṇaṃ tu paścimam .. 75.51 ..
75.d:
नानावर्णः स पार्श्वेषु पूर्वतः श्वेत उच्यते ।
पीतं च दक्षिणं तस्य भृङ्गवर्णं तु पश्चिमम् ॥ 75.51 ॥
75.m: It has various colors on its flanks: it is said to be white on the east, / yellow on its south, and the color of a bee on the west.

75.s:
uttaraṃ raktavarṇaṃ tu tasya pārśvaṃ mahātmanaḥ .
merustu śobhate śuklo rājavaṃśe tu dhiṣṭhitaḥ .. 75.52 ..
75.d:
उत्तरं रक्तवर्णं तु तस्य पार्श्वं महात्मनः ।
मेरुस्तु शोभते शुक्लो राजवंशे तु धिष्ठितः ॥ 75.52 ॥
75.m: And the northern flank of that great-souled one is red in color; / Meru shines bright, stationed in the royal lineage.

75.s:
taruṇādityasaṃkāśo vidhūma iva pāvakaḥ .
yojanānāṃ sahastrāṇi caturāśītirucchritaḥ .. 75.53 ..
75.d:
तरुणादित्यसंकाशो विधूम इव पावकः ।
योजनानां सहस्त्राणि चतुराशीतिरुच्छ्रितः ॥ 75.53 ॥
75.m: Resembling the morning sun, like a smokeless fire, / it is eighty-four thousand yojanas in height.

75.s:
praviṣṭaḥ ṣoḍaśādhastādvistṛtaḥ ṣoḍaśaiva tu .
śarāvasaṃsthitatvācca dvātriṃśanmūrdhni vistṛtaḥ .. 75.54 ..
75.d:
प्रविष्टः षोडशाधस्ताद्विस्तृतः षोडशैव तु ।
शरावसंस्थितत्वाच्च द्वात्रिंशन्मूर्ध्नि विस्तृतः ॥ 75.54 ॥
75.m: It penetrates sixteen [thousand] beneath and is sixteen [thousand] wide; / and because of being shaped like a shallow saucer, it is thirty-two [thousand] wide at the summit.

75.s:
vistārastriguṇaścāsya pariṇāhaḥ samantataḥ .
maṇḍalena pramāṇena vyasyamānaṃ tadiṣyate .. 75.55 ..
75.d:
विस्तारस्त्रिगुणश्चास्य परिणाहः समन्ततः ।
मण्डलेन प्रमाणेन व्यस्यमानं तदिष्यते ॥ 75.55 ॥
75.m: Its circumference all around is three times its diameter; / that is considered when calculated according to circular measurement.

75.s:
navatiśca sahastrāṇi yojanānāṃ samantataḥ .
tataḥ ṣaṭkādhikānāṃ ca vyasyamānaṃ prakīrttitam .
caturastreṇa mānena pariṇāhaḥ samantataḥ .. 75.56 ..
75.d:
नवतिश्च सहस्त्राणि योजनानां समन्ततः ।
ततः षट्काधिकानां च व्यस्यमानं प्रकीर्त्तितम् ।
चतुरस्त्रेण मानेन परिणाहः समन्ततः ॥ 75.56 ॥
75.m: Its circumference all around is proclaimed to be ninety thousand yojanas / plus six [thousand] more, when calculated / according to quadrangular measurement.

75.s:
sa parvato mahādivyo divyauṣadhisamanvitaḥ .
savanairāvṛtaḥ sarvo jātarūpamayaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 75.57 ..
75.d:
स पर्वतो महादिव्यो दिव्यौषधिसमन्वितः ।
सवनैरावृतः सर्वो जातरूपमयैः शुभैः ॥ 75.57 ॥
75.m: That mountain is exceedingly divine, endowed with divine medicinal herbs; / it is entirely covered with groves that are made of auspicious gold.

75.s:
tatra devagaṇāḥ sarve gandharvoragarākṣasāḥ .
śailarāje pramodante tathaivāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 75.58 ..
75.d:
तत्र देवगणाः सर्वे गन्धर्वोरगराक्षसाः ।
शैलराजे प्रमोदन्ते तथैवाप्सरसां गणाः ॥ 75.58 ॥
75.m:
There all the hosts of gods, Gandharvas, Uragas, and Rākṣasas,
rejoice upon that king of mountains, as do the troops of Apsarases.

75.s:
sa tu meruḥ parivṛto bhavanairbhūtabhāvanaiḥ .
catvāro yasya deśāstu nānāpārśveṣu dhiṣṭhitāḥ .. 75.59 ..
75.d:
स तु मेरुः परिवृतो भवनैर्भूतभावनैः ।
चत्वारो यस्य देशास्तु नानापार्श्वेषु धिष्ठिताः ॥ 75.59 ॥
75.m:
That Meru is surrounded by the dwellings of the source of beings,
and four realms are situated on its various sides:

75.s:
bhadrāśvo bhārataścaiva ketumālaśca paścime .
uttare kuravaścaiva kṛtapuṇyapratiśrayāḥ .. 75.60 ..
75.d:
भद्राश्वो भारतश्चैव केतुमालश्च पश्चिमे ।
उत्तरे कुरवश्चैव कृतपुण्यप्रतिश्रयाः ॥ 75.60 ॥
75.m:
Bhadrāśva, Bhārata, and Ketumāla in the west,
and the Kurus in the north, the refuges of meritorious deeds.

75.s:
karṇikā tasya padmasya samantāt parimaṇḍalā .
yojanānāṃ sahastrāṇi yojanānāṃ pramāṇataḥ .. 75.61 ..
75.d:
कर्णिका तस्य पद्मस्य समन्तात् परिमण्डला ।
योजनानां सहस्त्राणि योजनानां प्रमाणतः ॥ 75.61 ॥
75.m:
The pericarp of that lotus is circular all around,
thousands of yojanas in extent according to measurement.

75.s:
tasya kesarajālāni navaṣaṭ ca prakīrttitāḥ .
caturaśītirutsedho vivarāntaragocarāḥ .. 75.62 ..
75.d:
तस्य केसरजालानि नवषट् च प्रकीर्त्तिताः ।
चतुरशीतिरुत्सेधो विवरान्तरगोचराः ॥ 75.62 ॥
75.m:
Its network of filaments is declared to be fifty-four [in number];
its height is eighty-four [thousand yojanas], accessible through internal cavities.

75.s:
triṃśaccāpi sahastrāṇi yojanānāṃ pramāṇataḥ .
tasya kesarajālāni vikīrṇāni samantataḥ .. 75.63 ..
75.d:
त्रिंशच्चापि सहस्त्राणि योजनानां प्रमाणतः ।
तस्य केसरजालानि विकीर्णानि समन्ततः ॥ 75.63 ॥
75.m:
And thirty thousand yojanas in measurement
are its filaments scattered all around.

75.s:
śatasāhastramāyāmamaśītiḥ pṛthulāni ca .
catvāri tatra parṇāni yojanānāṃ caturdaśa .. 75.64 ..
75.d:
शतसाहस्त्रमायाममशीतिः पृथुलानि च ।
चत्वारि तत्र पर्णानि योजनानां चतुर्दश ॥ 75.64 ॥
75.m:
One hundred thousand [yojanas] in length, and eighty in width,
there are four petals there, measuring fourteen yojanas.

75.s:
tatra yā sā mayā tubhyaṃ karṇiketyabhiviśrutā .
tāṃ varṇyamānāmekāgryāt samāsena nibodhata .
maṇiparṇaśataiścitrāṃ nānāvarṇaprabhāsitām .. 75.65 ..
75.d:
तत्र या सा मया तुभ्यं कर्णिकेत्यभिविश्रुता ।
तां वर्ण्यमानामेकाग्र्यात् समासेन निबोधत ।
मणिपर्णशतैश्चित्रां नानावर्णप्रभासिताम् ॥ 75.65 ॥
75.m:
That which has been proclaimed to you as the pericarp—
listen attentively to that described in brief,
variegated with hundreds of jeweled petals, radiant with diverse colors,

75.s:
anekaparṇanicayaṃ sauvarṇamaruṇaprabham .
kāntaṃ sahastraparvāṇaṃ sahastrodarakandaram .
sahastraśatapatraṃ ca vṛttamekaṃ nagottamam .. 75.66 ..
75.d:
अनेकपर्णनिचयं सौवर्णमरुणप्रभम् ।
कान्तं सहस्त्रपर्वाणं सहस्त्रोदरकन्दरम् ।
सहस्त्रशतपत्रं च वृत्तमेकं नगोत्तमम् ॥ 75.66 ॥
75.m:
an accumulation of numerous petals, golden, shining like the dawn,
lovely, having a thousand joints, with a thousand internal caves,
having hundreds of thousands of petals, a single rounded, supreme mountain,

75.s:
maṇiratnārpitaśvabhrairmaṇibhiścitravedikam .
suvarṇamaṇicitrāṅgairmaṇicarcitatoraṇaiḥ .. 75.67 ..
75.d:
मणिरत्नार्पितश्वभ्रैर्मणिभिश्चित्रवेदिकम् ।
सुवर्णमणिचित्राङ्गैर्मणिचर्चिततोरणैः ॥ 75.67 ॥
75.m:
with chasms studded with gems and jewels, with altars variegated with jewels,
with bodies beautified by gold and jewels, and arched doorways adorned with jewels.

75.s:
tatra brahmasabhā ramyā brahmarṣijanasaṃkulā .
nāmnā manovratī nāma sarvalokeṣu viśrutā .. 75.68 ..
75.d:
तत्र ब्रह्मसभा रम्या ब्रह्मर्षिजनसंकुला ।
नाम्ना मनोव्रती नाम सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुता ॥ 75.68 ॥
75.m:
There stands the delightful assembly of Brahmā, crowded with brahmin seers,
celebrated in all the worlds by the name Manovratī.

75.s:
tatreśānasya devasya sahastrādityavarcasaḥ .
mahāvimānasaṃsthasya mahimā varttate sadā .. 75.69 ..
75.d:
तत्रेशानस्य देवस्य सहस्त्रादित्यवर्चसः ।
महाविमानसंस्थस्य महिमा वर्त्तते सदा ॥ 75.69 ॥
75.m:
There the greatness of the god Īśāna, endowed with the radiance of a thousand suns,
abiding in a great aerial chariot, always endures.

75.s:
tatra sarve devagaṇāścaturvaktraṃ svayaṃ prabhum .
iṣṭvā pūjyanamaskārairarcanīyamupasthitāḥ .. 75.70 ..
75.d:
तत्र सर्वे देवगणाश्चतुर्वक्त्रं स्वयं प्रभुम् ।
इष्ट्वा पूज्यनमस्कारैरर्चनीयमुपस्थिताः ॥ 75.70 ॥
75.m:
There all the hosts of gods have approached to honor the four-faced Lord himself,
having worshipped him with reverent salutations worthy of praise.

75.s:
yaistadā dihasaṃkalpairbrahmacaryaṃ mahātmabhiḥ .
cīrṇaṃ cārumanobhiśca sadācārapathi sthitaiḥ .. 75.71 ..
75.d:
यैस्तदा दिहसंकल्पैर्ब्रह्मचर्यं महात्मभिः ।
चीर्णं चारुमनोभिश्च सदाचारपथि स्थितैः ॥ 75.71 ॥
75.m:
By those great-souled ones of resolute purpose at that time,
celibate life was observed with beautiful minds, established on the path of good conduct.

75.s:
samyagiṣṭvā ca bhuktvā ca pitṛdevārcane ratāḥ .
gṛhāśramaparāstatra vinītā atithipriyāḥ .. 75.72 ..
75.d:
सम्यगिष्ट्वा च भुक्त्वा च पितृदेवार्चने रताः ।
गृहाश्रमपरास्तत्र विनीता अतिथिप्रियाः ॥ 75.72 ॥
75.m:
Having duly sacrificed and enjoyed, devoted to the worship of ancestors and gods,
devoted to the householder stage of life, humble and fond of guests,

75.s:
gṛhiṇaḥ śuklakarmasthā viraktāḥ kāraṇātmakāḥ .
yamairniyamadānaiśca dṛḍhanirdagdhakilbiṣāḥ .. 75.73 ..
75.d:
गृहिणः शुक्लकर्मस्था विरक्ताः कारणात्मकाः ।
यमैर्नियमदानैश्च दृढनिर्दग्धकिल्बिषाः ॥ 75.73 ॥
75.m:
householders engaged in pure deeds, dispassionate, established in discernment,
having completely burnt away sins through restraints, observances, and gifts—

75.s:
teṣāṃ nivasanaṃ śuklabrahmalokamaninditam .
uparyupari sarvāsāṃ gatīnāṃ paramā gatiḥ .
caturdaśasahastrāṇi yojanānāṃ tu kīrttitam .. 75.74 ..
75.d:
तेषां निवसनं शुक्लब्रह्मलोकमनिन्दितम् ।
उपर्युपरि सर्वासां गतीनां परमा गतिः ।
चतुर्दशसहस्त्राणि योजनानां तु कीर्त्तितम् ॥ 75.74 ॥

75.s:
tatorddharucire kṛṣṇe taruṇādityavarcasi .
mahāgirau tato ramye ratnadhātuvicitrite .. 75.75 ..
75.d:
ततोर्द्धरुचिरे कृष्णे तरुणादित्यवर्चसि ।
महागिरौ ततो रम्ये रत्नधातुविचित्रिते ॥ 75.75 ॥
75.m:
Then, on that high and beautiful [peak], dark yet brilliant as the morning sun,
on that great, delightful mountain variegated with jewels and minerals,

75.s:
naikaratnasamāvāse maṇitoraṇamandire .
meroḥ sarveṣu pārśveṣu samantāt parimaṇḍale .. 75.76 ..
75.d:
नैकरत्नसमावासे मणितोरणमन्दिरे ।
मेरोः सर्वेषु पार्श्वेषु समन्तात् परिमण्डले ॥ 75.76 ॥
75.m:
the dwelling of diverse gems, with temples having jeweled archways,
on all sides of Meru, forming a circle around it,

75.s:
triṃśadyojanasāhastraṃ cakrapāṭo nagottamaḥ .
jārudhiścaiva śailendra ityete uttarāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 75.77 ..
75.d:
त्रिंशद्योजनसाहस्त्रं चक्रपाटो नगोत्तमः ।
जारुधिश्चैव शैलेन्द्र इत्येते उत्तराः स्मृताः ॥ 75.77 ॥
75.m:
is Cakrapāṭa, the supreme mountain of thirty thousand yojanas,
and Jārudhi, the lord of mountains—these are remembered as the northern ones.

75.s:
eteṣāṃ śailamukhyānāmuttareṣu yathākramaḥ .
sthalīrantaradroṇyaśca sarāṃsi ca nibodhata .. 75.78 ..
75.d:
एतेषां शैलमुख्यानामुत्तरेषु यथाक्रमः ।
स्थलीरन्तरद्रोण्यश्च सरांसि च निबोधत ॥ 75.78 ॥
75.m:
In the north of these chief mountains, understand in due order
the tablelands, intermediate valleys, and lakes.

75.s:
daśayojanavistīrṇā cakrapāṭopanirgatā .
sā tūdrdhvavāhinī cāpi nadī bhūmau pratiṣṭhitā .. 75.79 ..
75.d:
दशयोजनविस्तीर्णा चक्रपाटोपनिर्गता ।
सा तूद्र्ध्ववाहिनी चापि नदी भूमौ प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ 75.79 ॥
75.m:
Ten yojanas wide, issuing from Cakrapāṭa,
flowing upwards, that river is also established upon the earth.

75.s:
sā puryāmamarāvatyāṃ kramamāṇendurā prabhau .
tayā tiraskṛtā vā'pi sūryendujyotiṣāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 75.80 ..
75.d:
सा पुर्याममरावत्यां क्रममाणेन्दुरा प्रभौ ।
तया तिरस्कृता वाऽपि सूर्येन्दुज्योतिषां गणाः ॥ 75.80 ॥
75.m:
She proceeds into the city of Amarāvatī, resplendent like the moon;
by her the hosts of the lights of the sun and moon are surpassed.

75.s:
udayāstamite sandhye ye sevante dvijottamāḥ .
tān tuṣyante dvijāḥ sarvānaṣṭāvapyacalottamān .. 75.81 ..
75.d:
उदयास्तमिते सन्ध्ये ये सेवन्ते द्विजोत्तमाः ।
तान् तुष्यन्ते द्विजाः सर्वानष्टावप्यचलोत्तमान् ॥ 75.81 ॥
75.m:
Those excellent twice-born who worship at the twilights of sunrise and sunset,
those twice-born please all eight supreme mountains.

75.s: paribhramajjyotiṣāṃ yā sā rudrendramatā śubhā .. 75.82 ..
75.d: परिभ्रमज्ज्योतिषां या सा रुद्रेन्द्रमता शुभा ॥ 75.82 ॥
75.m: That auspicious [river], regarded by Rudra and Indra, belongs to the revolving heavenly bodies.

75.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre pañcasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 75 ..
75.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे पञ्चसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 75 ॥
75.m: Thus ends the seventy-fifth chapter in the holy Varāhapurāṇa, an authoritative scripture of the Lord.

76.s:
rudra uvāca .
tasyaiva meroḥ pūrve tu deśe paramavarcase .
cakravāṭaparikṣipte nānādhātuvirājite .. 76.1 ..
76.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
तस्यैव मेरोः पूर्वे तु देशे परमवर्चसे ।
चक्रवाटपरिक्षिप्ते नानाधातुविराजिते ॥ 76.1 ॥
76.m:
Rudra said:
In the eastern region of that very Meru, of supreme splendor,
surrounded by the mountain ring and adorned with various minerals,

76.s:
tatra sarvāmarapuraṃ cakravāṭasamuddhatam .
durdharṣaṃ baladṛptānāṃ devadānavarakṣasām .
tatra jāmbūnadamayaḥ suprākāraḥ sutoraṇaḥ .. 76.2 ..
76.d:
तत्र सर्वामरपुरं चक्रवाटसमुद्धतम् ।
दुर्धर्षं बलदृप्तानां देवदानवरक्षसाम् ।
तत्र जाम्बूनदमयः सुप्राकारः सुतोरणः ॥ 76.2 ॥

76.s:
tasyāpyuttarapūrve tu deśe paramavarcase .
alokajanasaṃpūrṇā vimānaśatasaṃkulā .. 76.3 ..
76.d:
तस्याप्युत्तरपूर्वे तु देशे परमवर्चसे ।
अलोकजनसंपूर्णा विमानशतसंकुला ॥ 76.3 ॥
76.m:
In its north-eastern direction, of supreme luster,
filled with invisible beings and crowded with hundreds of aerial cars,

76.s:
mahāvāpisamāyuktā nityaṃ pramuditā śubhā .
śobhitā puṣpaśabalaiḥ patākādhvajamālinī .. 76.4 ..
76.d:
महावापिसमायुक्ता नित्यं प्रमुदिता शुभा ।
शोभिता पुष्पशबलैः पताकाध्वजमालिनी ॥ 76.4 ॥
76.m:
endowed with great reservoirs, ever joyous and auspicious,
adorned with multicolored flowers, garlanded with banners and flags,

76.s:
devairyakṣopsarobhiśca ṛṣibhiśca suśobhitā .
purandarapurī ramyā samṛddhā tvamarāvatī .. 76.5 ..
76.d:
देवैर्यक्षोप्सरोभिश्च ऋषिभिश्च सुशोभिता ।
पुरन्दरपुरी रम्या समृद्धा त्वमरावती ॥ 76.5 ॥
76.m:
beautifully adorned by gods, Yakṣas, Apsarases, and ṛṣis,
is the delightful and prosperous Amarāvatī, the city of Indra.

76.s:
tasyā madhye'marāvatyā vajravaidūryavedikā .
trailokyaguṇavikhyātā sudharmā nāma vai sabhā .. 76.6 ..
76.d:
तस्या मध्येऽमरावत्या वज्रवैदूर्यवेदिका ।
त्रैलोक्यगुणविख्याता सुधर्मा नाम वै सभा ॥ 76.6 ॥
76.m:
In the midst of that Amarāvatī stands an altar of diamond and cat's-eye,
and the assembly hall named Sudharmā, renowned for its virtues across the three worlds.

76.s:
tatrāste śrīpateḥ śrīmān sahastrākṣaḥ śacīpatiḥ .
siddhādibhiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvābhirdevayonibhiḥ .. 76.7 ..
76.d:
तत्रास्ते श्रीपतेः श्रीमान् सहस्त्राक्षः शचीपतिः ।
सिद्धादिभिः परिवृतः सर्वाभिर्देवयोनिभिः ॥ 76.7 ॥
76.m:
There sits the glorious husband of Śacī, the thousand-eyed lord of fortune,
surrounded by Siddhas and others, and by all classes of divine beings.

76.s:
tatra caiva suvaṃśaḥ syād bhāskarasya mahātmanaḥ .
sākṣāt tatra surādhyakṣaḥ sarvadevanamaskṛtaḥ .. 76.8 ..
76.d:
तत्र चैव सुवंशः स्याद् भास्करस्य महात्मनः ।
साक्षात् तत्र सुराध्यक्षः सर्वदेवनमस्कृतः ॥ 76.8 ॥
76.m:
There is also the noble lineage of the great-souled sun;
in person there is the ruler of gods, worshipped by all the celestials.

76.s:
tasyāśca dikṣu vistīrṇā tattadguṇasamanvitā .
tejovatī nāma purī hutāśasya mahātmanaḥ .. 76.9 ..
76.d:
तस्याश्च दिक्षु विस्तीर्णा तत्तद्गुणसमन्विता ।
तेजोवती नाम पुरी हुताशस्य महात्मनः ॥ 76.9 ॥
76.m:
In its directions lies the extensive city endowed with various virtues,
named Tejovatī, belonging to the great-souled fire god.

76.s:
tattadguṇavatī ramyā purī vaivasvatasya ca .
nāmnā saṃyamanī nāma purī trailokyaviśrutā .. 76.10 ..
76.d:
तत्तद्गुणवती रम्या पुरी वैवस्वतस्य च ।
नाम्ना संयमनी नाम पुरी त्रैलोक्यविश्रुता ॥ 76.10 ॥
76.m:
Endowed with various merits is the delightful city of the son of Vivasvat,
named Saṃyamanī, celebrated throughout the three worlds.

76.s:
tathā caturthe digbhāge nairṛtādhipateḥ śubhā .
nāmnā kṛṣṇāvatī nāma virūpākṣasya dhīmataḥ .. 76.11 ..
76.d:
तथा चतुर्थे दिग्भागे नैरृताधिपतेः शुभा ।
नाम्ना कृष्णावती नाम विरूपाक्षस्य धीमतः ॥ 76.11 ॥
76.m:
Likewise, in the fourth quarter is the auspicious city of the lord of the south-west,
named Kṛṣṇāvatī, belonging to the wise Virūpākṣa.

76.s:
pañcame hyuttarapuṭe nāmnā śuddhavatī purī .
udakādhipateḥ khyātā varuṇasya mahātmanaḥ .. 76.12 ..
76.d:
पञ्चमे ह्युत्तरपुटे नाम्ना शुद्धवती पुरी ।
उदकाधिपतेः ख्याता वरुणस्य महात्मनः ॥ 76.12 ॥
76.m:
In the fifth, the northern precinct, is the city named Śuddhavatī,
renowned as belonging to the great-souled Varuṇa, lord of waters.

76.s:
tathā pañcottare devasvasyottarapuṭe purī .
vāyorgandhavatī nāma khyātā sarvaguṇottarā .. 76.13 ..
76.d:
तथा पञ्चोत्तरे देवस्वस्योत्तरपुटे पुरी ।
वायोर्गन्धवती नाम ख्याता सर्वगुणोत्तरा ॥ 76.13 ॥
76.m:
Likewise, in the fifth northern precinct of the god is the city
of Vāyu, named Gandhavatī, celebrated as superior in all virtues.

76.s:
tasyottarapuṭe ramyā guhyakādhipateḥ purī .
nāmnā mahodayā nāma śubhā vaidūryavedikā .. 76.14 ..
76.d:
तस्योत्तरपुटे रम्या गुह्यकाधिपतेः पुरी ।
नाम्ना महोदया नाम शुभा वैदूर्यवेदिका ॥ 76.14 ॥
76.m:
In the northern precinct beyond that is the delightful city of the lord of Guhyakas,
named Mahodayā, auspicious, with an altar of cat's-eye.

76.s:
tathāṣṭame'ntarapuṭe īśānasya mahātmanaḥ .
purī manoharā nāma bhūtairnānāvidhairyutā .
puṣpairdhanyaiśca vividhairvanairāśramasaṃsthitaiḥ .. 76.15 ..
76.d:
तथाष्टमेऽन्तरपुटे ईशानस्य महात्मनः ।
पुरी मनोहरा नाम भूतैर्नानाविधैर्युता ।
पुष्पैर्धन्यैश्च विविधैर्वनैराश्रमसंस्थितैः ॥ 76.15 ॥
76.m:
Likewise, in the eighth intermediate precinct is that of the great-souled Īśāna,
the city named Manoharā, filled with various kinds of spirits,
with varied noble flowers and forests housing hermitages.

76.s: prārthyate devaloko'yaṃ sa svarga iti kīrtitaḥ .. 76.16 ..
76.d: प्रार्थ्यते देवलोकोऽयं स स्वर्ग इति कीर्तितः ॥ 76.16 ॥
76.m: This world of the gods is sought after; it is proclaimed as heaven.
Thus ends the seventy-sixth chapter in the holy Varāhapurāṇa, an authoritative scripture of the Lord.

77.s:
rudra uvāca .
yadetat karṇikāmūlaṃ merormadhyaṃ prakīrtitam .
tad yojanasahastrāṇi saṃkhyayā mānataḥ smṛtam .. 77.1 ..
77.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
यदेतत् कर्णिकामूलं मेरोर्मध्यं प्रकीर्तितम् ।
तद् योजनसहस्त्राणि संख्यया मानतः स्मृतम् ॥ 77.1 ॥
77.m:
Rudra said:
That base of the pericarp which is proclaimed as the middle of Meru,
is remembered as measuring thousands of yojanas in calculation.

77.s:
catvāriṃśat tathā cāṣṭau sahastrāṇi tu maṇḍalaiḥ .
śailarājasya tattatra merumūlamiti smṛtam .. 77.2 ..
77.d:
चत्वारिंशत् तथा चाष्टौ सहस्त्राणि तु मण्डलैः ।
शैलराजस्य तत्तत्र मेरुमूलमिति स्मृतम् ॥ 77.2 ॥
77.m: And forty-eight thousand [yojanas] in circumference— / that is known as the base of Meru, the king of mountains, there.

77.s:
teṣāṃ girisahastrāṇāmanekānāṃ mahocchrayaḥ .
digaṣṭau ca punastasya maryādāparvatāḥ śubhāḥ .. 77.3 ..
77.d:
तेषां गिरिसहस्त्राणामनेकानां महोच्छ्रयः ।
दिगष्टौ च पुनस्तस्य मर्यादापर्वताः शुभाः ॥ 77.3 ॥
77.m: The immense height of those many thousands of mountains [is described]; / and furthermore, in its eight directions, there are auspicious boundary-mountains.

77.s:
jaṭharo devakūṭaśca pūrvasyāṃ diśi parvatau .
pūrvapaścāyatāvetāvarṇavāntarvyavasthitau .
maryādāparvatānetānaṣṭānāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ .. 77.4 ..
77.d:
जठरो देवकूटश्च पूर्वस्यां दिशि पर्वतौ ।
पूर्वपश्चायतावेतावर्णवान्तर्व्यवस्थितौ ।
मर्यादापर्वतानेतानष्टानाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥ 77.4 ॥
77.m: Jaṭhara and Devakūṭa are the two mountains in the eastern direction; / extending from east to west, these two are situated within the ocean. / The wise declare these eight boundary-mountains.

77.s:
yo'sau merurdvijaśreṣṭhāḥ proktaḥ kanakaparvataḥ .
viṣkambhāṃstasya vakṣyāmi śrṛṇudhvaṃ gadatastu tān .. 77.5 ..
77.d:
योऽसौ मेरुर्द्विजश्रेष्ठाः प्रोक्तः कनकपर्वतः ।
विष्कम्भांस्तस्य वक्ष्यामि श्रृणुध्वं गदतस्तु तान् ॥ 77.5 ॥
77.m: O best of the twice-born, concerning this Meru, spoken of as the golden mountain, / I will declare its buttress-mountains; listen as I describe them:

77.s:
mahāpādāstu catvāro meroratha caturdiśam .
yairna cacāla viṣṭabdhā saptadvīpavatī mahī .. 77.6 ..
77.d:
महापादास्तु चत्वारो मेरोरथ चतुर्दिशम् ।
यैर्न चचाल विष्टब्धा सप्तद्वीपवती मही ॥ 77.6 ॥
77.m: There are four great foothills of Meru in the four directions, / supported by which the Earth, possessing seven continents, did not shake.

77.s:
daśayojanasāhastraṃ vyāyāmasteṣu śaṅkyate .
tiryagūrdhvaṃ ca racitā haritālataṭairvṛtāḥ .. 77.7 ..
77.d:
दशयोजनसाहस्त्रं व्यायामस्तेषु शङ्क्यते ।
तिर्यगूर्ध्वं च रचिता हरितालतटैर्वृताः ॥ 77.7 ॥
77.m: Their extent is estimated to be ten thousand yojanas; / fashioned horizontally and vertically, they are covered with slopes of yellow orpiment,

77.s:
manaḥśilādarībhiśca suvarṇamaṇicitritāḥ .'
anekasiddhabhavanaiḥ krīḍāsthānaiśca suprabhāḥ .. 77.8 ..
77.d:
मनःशिलादरीभिश्च सुवर्णमणिचित्रिताः ।'
अनेकसिद्धभवनैः क्रीडास्थानैश्च सुप्रभाः ॥ 77.8 ॥
77.m: and with caves of realgar, variegated with gold and jewels, / shining brightly with dwellings of numerous Siddhas and places of sport.

77.s:
pūrveṇa mandarastasya dakṣiṇe gandhamādanaḥ .
vipulaḥ paścime pārśve supārśvaścottare sthitaḥ .. 77.9 ..
77.d:
पूर्वेण मन्दरस्तस्य दक्षिणे गन्धमादनः ।
विपुलः पश्चिमे पार्श्वे सुपार्श्वश्चोत्तरे स्थितः ॥ 77.9 ॥
77.m: To its east is Mandara, to the south is Gandhamādana, / Vipula is on the western flank, and Supārśva stands to the north.

77.s:
teṣāṃ śrṛṅgeṣu catvāro mahāvṛkṣāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ .
devadaityāpsarobhiśca sevitā guṇasaṃcayaiḥ .. 77.10 ..
77.d:
तेषां श्रृङ्गेषु चत्वारो महावृक्षाः प्रतिष्ठिताः ।
देवदैत्याप्सरोभिश्च सेविता गुणसंचयैः ॥ 77.10 ॥
77.m: Upon their peaks stand four great trees, / frequented by gods, daityas, and apsarases, endowed with an abundance of virtues.

77.s:
mandarasya gireḥ śrṛṅge kadambo nāma pādapaḥ .
pralambaśākhāśikharaḥ kadambaścaityapādapaḥ .. 77.11 ..
77.d:
मन्दरस्य गिरेः श्रृङ्गे कदम्बो नाम पादपः ।
प्रलम्बशाखाशिखरः कदम्बश्चैत्यपादपः ॥ 77.11 ॥
77.m: On the peak of Mount Mandara stands the tree named Kadamba, / a sacred caitya tree, its crown bearing hanging branches,

77.s:
mahākumbhapramāṇaiśca puṣpairvikacakesaraiḥ .
mahāgandhamanojñaiśca śobhitaḥ sarvakālajaiḥ .. 77.12 ..
77.d:
महाकुम्भप्रमाणैश्च पुष्पैर्विकचकेसरैः ।
महागन्धमनोज्ञैश्च शोभितः सर्वकालजैः ॥ 77.12 ॥
77.m: adorned with flowers as large as great water-jars, with blossoming filaments, / charming with great fragrance, blossoming in all seasons,

77.s:
samāsena parivṛto bhuvanairbhūtabhāvanaiḥ .
sahastramadhikaṃ so'tha gandhenāpūrayan diśaḥ .. 77.13 ..
77.d:
समासेन परिवृतो भुवनैर्भूतभावनैः ।
सहस्त्रमधिकं सोऽथ गन्धेनापूरयन् दिशः ॥ 77.13 ॥
77.m: completely surrounded by the worlds that bring forth creatures, / filling the directions with its fragrance for more than a thousand [yojanas].

77.s:
bhadrāśvo nāma vṛkṣo'yaṃ varṣādreḥ ketusaṃbhavaḥ .
kīrtimān rūpavāñchrīmān mahāpādapapādapaḥ .
yatra sākṣāddhṛṣīkeśaḥ siddhasaṅghairniṣevyate .. 77.14 ..
77.d:
भद्राश्वो नाम वृक्षोऽयं वर्षाद्रेः केतुसंभवः ।
कीर्तिमान् रूपवाञ्छ्रीमान् महापादपपादपः ।
यत्र साक्षाद्धृषीकेशः सिद्धसङ्घैर्निषेव्यते ॥ 77.14 ॥
77.m: This tree is Bhadrāśva, the banner of that region-mountain; / famous, shapely, glorious, a tree that is a great tree, / where Hṛṣīkeśa is worshipped directly by hosts of Siddhas.

77.s:
tasya bhadrakadambasya tathāśvavadano hariḥ .
prāptavāṃścāmaraśreṣṭhaḥ sa hi sānuṃ punaḥ punaḥ .. 77.15 ..
77.d:
तस्य भद्रकदम्बस्य तथाश्ववदनो हरिः ।
प्राप्तवांश्चामरश्रेष्ठः स हि सानुं पुनः पुनः ॥ 77.15 ॥
77.m: Unto that Bhadrakadamba, Hari with the horse's face, / the foremost of immortals, came repeatedly to its peak.

77.s:
tena cālokitaṃ varṣaṃ sarvadvipadanāyakāḥ .
yasya nāmnā samākhyāto bhadrāśveti na saṃśayaḥ .. 77.16 ..
77.d:
तेन चालोकितं वर्षं सर्वद्विपदनायकाः ।
यस्य नाम्ना समाख्यातो भद्राश्वेति न संशयः ॥ 77.16 ॥
77.m: And by him the realm was surveyed, O leaders of all bipeds; / after whose name it is declared as Bhadrāśva, beyond doubt.

77.s:
dakṣiṇasyāpi śailasya śikhare devasevite .
jambūḥ sadyaḥ puṣpaphalā mahāśākhopaśobhitā .. 77.17 ..
77.d:
दक्षिणस्यापि शैलस्य शिखरे देवसेविते ।
जम्बूः सद्यः पुष्पफला महाशाखोपशोभिता ॥ 77.17 ॥
77.m: On the peak of the southern mountain also, frequented by the gods, / is the Jambū tree, instantly flowering and fruiting, adorned with huge branches.

77.s:
tasyā hyatipramāṇāni svādūni ca mṛdūni ca .
phalānyamṛtakalpāni patanti girimūrdhani .. 77.18 ..
77.d:
तस्या ह्यतिप्रमाणानि स्वादूनि च मृदूनि च ।
फलान्यमृतकल्पानि पतन्ति गिरिमूर्धनि ॥ 77.18 ॥
77.m: Indeed, its sweet, soft, enormous fruits, / resembling nectar, fall upon the summit of the mountain.

77.s:
tasmād girivaraśreṣṭhāt phalaprasyandavāhinī .
divyā jāmbūnadī nāma pravṛttā madhuvāhinī .. 77.19 ..
77.d:
तस्माद् गिरिवरश्रेष्ठात् फलप्रस्यन्दवाहिनी ।
दिव्या जाम्बूनदी नाम प्रवृत्ता मधुवाहिनी ॥ 77.19 ॥
77.m: From that best of excellent mountains flows / the celestial river named Jāmbūnadī, carrying the flow of fruits, carrying nectar.

77.s:
tatra jāmbūnadaṃ nāma suvarṇamanalaprabham .
devālaṅkāramatulamutpannaṃ pāpanāśanam .. 77.20 ..
77.d:
तत्र जाम्बूनदं नाम सुवर्णमनलप्रभम् ।
देवालङ्कारमतुलमुत्पन्नं पापनाशनम् ॥ 77.20 ॥
77.m: There the gold named Jāmbūnada, radiant like fire, / peerless ornament of the gods, destroyer of sins, came into being.

77.s:
devadānavagandharvayakṣarākṣasaguhyakāḥ .
papustadamṛtaprakhyaṃ madhu jambūphalasravam .. 77.21 ..
77.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वयक्षराक्षसगुह्यकाः ।
पपुस्तदमृतप्रख्यं मधु जम्बूफलस्रवम् ॥ 77.21 ॥
77.m: Gods, dānavas, gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and guhyakas / drank that nectar-like juice flowing from the jambū fruit.

77.s:
sā keturdakṣiṇe varṣe jambūrlokeṣu viśrutā .
yasyā nāmnā samākhyātā jambūdvīpeti mānavaiḥ .. 77.22 ..
77.d:
सा केतुर्दक्षिणे वर्षे जम्बूर्लोकेषु विश्रुता ।
यस्या नाम्ना समाख्याता जम्बूद्वीपेति मानवैः ॥ 77.22 ॥
77.m: That Jambū, renowned in the worlds, is the banner of the southern realm, / after whose name it is called Jambūdvīpa by men.

77.s:
vipulasya ca śailasya dakṣiṇena mahātmanaḥ .
jātaḥ śrṛṅgeti sumahānaśvatthaśceti pādapaḥ .. 77.23 ..
77.d:
विपुलस्य च शैलस्य दक्षिणेन महात्मनः ।
जातः श्रृङ्गेति सुमहानश्वत्थश्चेति पादपः ॥ 77.23 ॥
77.m: To the south of the great mountain Vipula, / a very great aśvattha tree named Śṛṅgī arose,

77.s:
mahocchrāyo mahāskandho naikasattvaguṇālayaḥ .
kumbhapramāṇai ruciraiḥ phalaiḥ sarvarttukaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 77.24 ..
77.d:
महोच्छ्रायो महास्कन्धो नैकसत्त्वगुणालयः ।
कुम्भप्रमाणै रुचिरैः फलैः सर्वर्त्तुकैः शुभैः ॥ 77.24 ॥
77.m: of great height and huge trunk, the abode of many sattva-qualities, / with delightful, auspicious fruits of every season, the size of water-jars.

77.s:
sa ketuḥ ketumālānāṃ devagandharvasevitaḥ .
ketumāleti vikhyāto nāmnā tatra prakīrtitaḥ .
tannibodhata viprendrā niruktaṃ nāmakarmaṇaḥ .. 77.25 ..
77.d:
स केतुः केतुमालानां देवगन्धर्वसेवितः ।
केतुमालेति विख्यातो नाम्ना तत्र प्रकीर्तितः ।
तन्निबोधत विप्रेन्द्रा निरुक्तं नामकर्मणः ॥ 77.25 ॥
77.m: It is the banner of the Ketumālas, frequented by gods and gandharvas, / known there by the name Ketumāla. / Hear, O foremost of sages, the etymology of that name and deed:

77.s:
kṣīrodamathane vṛtte mālā skandhe niveśitāḥ .
indreṇa caityaketostu ketumālastataḥ smṛtaḥ .
tena taccihnitaṃ varṣaṃ ketumāleti viśrutam .. 77.26 ..
77.d:
क्षीरोदमथने वृत्ते माला स्कन्धे निवेशिताः ।
इन्द्रेण चैत्यकेतोस्तु केतुमालस्ततः स्मृतः ।
तेन तच्चिह्नितं वर्षं केतुमालेति विश्रुतम् ॥ 77.26 ॥
77.m: When the churning of the milk ocean occurred, garlands were placed on its trunk / by Indra; hence the caitya banner is remembered as Ketumāla. / Marked by it, that realm is known as Ketumāla.

77.s:
supārśvasyottare śrṛṅge vaṭo nāma mahādrumaḥ .
nyagrodho vipulaskandho yastriyojanamaṇḍalaḥ .. 77.27 ..
77.d:
सुपार्श्वस्योत्तरे श्रृङ्गे वटो नाम महाद्रुमः ।
न्यग्रोधो विपुलस्कन्धो यस्त्रियोजनमण्डलः ॥ 77.27 ॥
77.m: On the northern peak of Supārśva is a great banyan tree named Vaṭa, / a nyagrodha with a massive trunk, whose canopy covers three yojanas,

77.s:
mālyadāmakalāpaiśca vividhaistu samantataḥ .
śākhābhirlambamānābhiḥ śobhitaḥ siddhasevitaḥ .. 77.28 ..
77.d:
माल्यदामकलापैश्च विविधैस्तु समन्ततः ।
शाखाभिर्लम्बमानाभिः शोभितः सिद्धसेवितः ॥ 77.28 ॥
77.m: adorned on all sides with collections of various garlands, / with hanging branches, frequented by Siddhas,

77.s:
pralambakumbhasadṛśairhemavarṇaiḥ phalaiḥ sadā .
sa hyuttarakurūṇāṃ tu ketuvṛkṣaḥ prakāśate .. 77.29 ..
77.d:
प्रलम्बकुम्भसदृशैर्हेमवर्णैः फलैः सदा ।
स ह्युत्तरकुरूणां तु केतुवृक्षः प्रकाशते ॥ 77.29 ॥
77.m: always with gold-colored fruits resembling hanging water-jars; / it indeed shines as the banner-tree of the Uttarakurus.

77.s:
sanatkumārāvarajā mānasā brahmaṇaḥ sutāḥ .
sapta tatra mahābhāgāḥ kuravo nāma viśrutāḥ .. 77.30 ..
77.d:
सनत्कुमारावरजा मानसा ब्रह्मणः सुताः ।
सप्त तत्र महाभागाः कुरवो नाम विश्रुताः ॥ 77.30 ॥
77.m: The seven mind-born sons of Brahmā, younger brothers of Sanatkumāra, / highly fortunate, are renowned there as the Kurus.

77.s:
tatra sthiragatairjñānairvirajaskairmahātmabhiḥ .
akṣayaḥ kṣayaparyanto lokaḥ proktaḥ sanātanaḥ .. 77.31 ..
77.d:
तत्र स्थिरगतैर्ज्ञानैर्विरजस्कैर्महात्मभिः ।
अक्षयः क्षयपर्यन्तो लोकः प्रोक्तः सनातनः ॥ 77.31 ॥
77.m: There, by those great souls of steady knowledge, free from passion, / that eternal realm, imperishable until the time of destruction, was proclaimed.

77.s:
teṣāṃ nāmāṅkitaṃ varṣaṃ saptānāṃ vai mahātmanām .
divi ceha ca vikhyātā uttarāḥ kuravaḥ sadā .. 77.32 ..
77.d:
तेषां नामाङ्कितं वर्षं सप्तानां वै महात्मनाम् ।
दिवि चेह च विख्याता उत्तराः कुरवः सदा ॥ 77.32 ॥
77.m: The realm is marked with the names of those seven great souls; / Uttarakuru is ever renowned in heaven and on earth.

77.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre saptasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 77 ..
77.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे सप्तसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 77 ॥
77.m: Thus ends the seventy-seventh chapter in the venerable Varāha Purāṇa, a scripture of the Lord.

78.s:
rudra uvāca .
tathā caturṇāṃ vakṣyāmi śailendrāṇāṃ yathākramam .
anuvidhyāni ramyāṇi vihaṅgaiḥ kūjitāni ca .. 78.1 ..
78.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
तथा चतुर्णां वक्ष्यामि शैलेन्द्राणां यथाक्रमम् ।
अनुविध्यानि रम्याणि विहङ्गैः कूजितानि च ॥ 78.1 ॥
78.m: Rudra said: / So also I will declare in order the four mountain-rulers' / pleasant surrounding regions, made resonant by the chirping of birds,

78.s:
anekapakṣiyuktātmaśrṛṅgāṇi subahūni ca .
devānāṃ divyanārībhiḥ samaṃ krīḍāmayāni ca .. 78.2 ..
78.d:
अनेकपक्षियुक्तात्मश्रृङ्गाणि सुबहूनि च ।
देवानां दिव्यनारीभिः समं क्रीडामयानि च ॥ 78.2 ॥
78.m: having very many peaks filled with numerous birds, / places of sport for gods together with divine women,

78.s:
kinnarodgītaghuṣṭāni śītamandasugandhibhiḥ .
pavanaiḥ sevyamānāni ramaṇīyatarāṇi ca .. 78.3 ..
78.d:
किन्नरोद्गीतघुष्टानि शीतमन्दसुगन्धिभिः ।
पवनैः सेव्यमानानि रमणीयतराणि च ॥ 78.3 ॥
78.m: echoing with the loud singing of Kinnaras, visited / by cool, gentle, fragrant breezes, and extremely delightful.

78.s:
caturddikṣu virājante nāmataḥ śrṛṇutānaghāḥ .
pūrve caitrarathaṃ nāma dakṣiṇe gandhamādanam .
prabhāveṇa sutoyāni navakhaṇḍayutāni ca .. 78.4 ..
78.d:
चतुर्द्दिक्षु विराजन्ते नामतः श्रृणुतानघाः ।
पूर्वे चैत्ररथं नाम दक्षिणे गन्धमादनम् ।
प्रभावेण सुतोयानि नवखण्डयुतानि च ॥ 78.4 ॥
78.m: They shine in the four directions; hear them by name, O sinless ones: / in the east is the one named Caitraratha, in the south is Gandhamādana, / possessing excellent waters and nine divisions by their power;

78.s:
vanaṣaṇḍāṃstathākramya devatā lalanāyutāḥ .
yatra krīḍanti coddeśe mudā paramayā yutāḥ .. 78.5 ..
78.d:
वनषण्डांस्तथाक्रम्य देवता ललनायुताः ।
यत्र क्रीडन्ति चोद्देशे मुदा परमया युताः ॥ 78.5 ॥
78.m: and reaching the groves of trees, the deities accompanied by beautiful women / sport in that region, filled with supreme joy.

78.s:
anubandhāni ramyāṇi vihagaiḥ kūjitāni ca .
ratnopakīrṇatirthāni mahāpuṇyajalāni ca .. 78.6 ..
78.d:
अनुबन्धानि रम्याणि विहगैः कूजितानि च ।
रत्नोपकीर्णतिर्थानि महापुण्यजलानि च ॥ 78.6 ॥
78.m: They have charming continuous tracts, filled with bird-calls, / bathing places strewn with gems, and waters of great merit,

78.s:
anekajalayantraiśca nāditāni mahānti ca .
śākhābhirlambamānābhī ruvatpakṣikulālibhiḥ .. 78.7 ..
78.d:
अनेकजलयन्त्रैश्च नादितानि महान्ति च ।
शाखाभिर्लम्बमानाभी रुवत्पक्षिकुलालिभिः ॥ 78.7 ॥
78.m: resounding with numerous waterworks, large, / with drooping branches, humming with swarms of birds and bees.

78.s:
kamalotpalakahlāraśobhitāni sarāṃsi ca .
caturṣu teṣu giriṣu nānāguṇayuteṣu ca .. 78.8 ..
78.d:
कमलोत्पलकह्लारशोभितानि सरांसि च ।
चतुर्षु तेषु गिरिषु नानागुणयुतेषु च ॥ 78.8 ॥
78.m: And there are lakes adorned with lotuses, blue water-lilies, and white water-lilies, / upon those four mountains endowed with various virtues:

78.s:
aruṇodaṃ tu pūrveṇa dakṣiṇe mānasaṃ smṛtam .
asitodaṃ paścime ca mahābhadraṃ tathottare .
kumudaiḥ śvetakapilaiḥ kahlārairbhūṣitāni ca .. 78.9 ..
78.d:
अरुणोदं तु पूर्वेण दक्षिणे मानसं स्मृतम् ।
असितोदं पश्चिमे च महाभद्रं तथोत्तरे ।
कुमुदैः श्वेतकपिलैः कह्लारैर्भूषितानि च ॥ 78.9 ॥
78.m: Aruṇoda is known in the east, Mānasa in the south, / Asitoda in the west, and Mahābhadra in the north, / adorned with white and tawny lotuses and white water-lilies.

78.s:
aruṇodayasya ye śailāḥ prācyā vai nāmataḥ smṛtāḥ .
tān kīrttyamānāṃstattvena śrṛṇudhvaṃ gadato mama .. 78.10 ..
78.d:
अरुणोदयस्य ये शैलाः प्राच्या वै नामतः स्मृताः ।
तान् कीर्त्त्यमानांस्तत्त्वेन श्रृणुध्वं गदतो मम ॥ 78.10 ॥
78.m: Hear from me as I accurately declare the names / of those eastern mountains of Aruṇoda as they are recounted.

78.s:
vikaṅko maṇiśrṛṅgaśca supātraścopalo mahān .
mahānīlo'tha kumbhaśca subindurmadanastathā .. 78.11 ..
78.d:
विकङ्को मणिश्रृङ्गश्च सुपात्रश्चोपलो महान् ।
महानीलोऽथ कुम्भश्च सुबिन्दुर्मदनस्तथा ॥ 78.11 ॥
78.m: Vikaṅka, Maṇiśṛṅga, Supātra, the great Upala, / Mahānīla, Kumbha, Subindu, and Madana,

78.s:
veṇunaddhaḥ sumedāśca niṣadho devaparvataḥ .
ityete parvatavarāḥ puṇyāśca girayo'pare .. 78.12 ..
78.d:
वेणुनद्धः सुमेदाश्च निषधो देवपर्वतः ।
इत्येते पर्वतवराः पुण्याश्च गिरयोऽपरे ॥ 78.12 ॥
78.m: Veṇunaddha, Sumeda, Niṣadha, and Devaparvata— / these are the best of mountains, and there are other sacred mountains.

78.s:
pūrveṇa mandarāt siddhāḥ parvatāśca madāyutāḥ .
saraso mānasasyeha dakṣiṇena mahācalāḥ .. 78.13 ..
78.d:
पूर्वेण मन्दरात् सिद्धाः पर्वताश्च मदायुताः ।
सरसो मानसस्येह दक्षिणेन महाचलाः ॥ 78.13 ॥
78.m: To the east of Mandara are mountains attended by the Siddhas and filled with intoxication. / To the south of Lake Mānasa here are great mountains,

78.s:
ye kīrttitā mayā tubhyaṃ nāmatastān nibodhata .
śailastriśiraścaiva śiśiraścācalottamaḥ .. 78.14 ..
78.d:
ये कीर्त्तिता मया तुभ्यं नामतस्तान् निबोधत ।
शैलस्त्रिशिरश्चैव शिशिरश्चाचलोत्तमः ॥ 78.14 ॥
78.m: which have been mentioned by me to you; learn them by name: / The mountain Triśiras, and Śiśira, the best of mountains,

78.s:
kapiśca śatamakṣaśca turagaścaiva sānumān .
tāmrāhaśca viṣaścaiva tathā śvetodano giriḥ .. 78.15 ..
78.d:
कपिश्च शतमक्षश्च तुरगश्चैव सानुमान् ।
ताम्राहश्च विषश्चैव तथा श्वेतोदनो गिरिः ॥ 78.15 ॥
78.m: Kapi, Śatamakṣa, Turaga, the peaked Sānumān, / Tāmrāha, Viṣa, and likewise the mountain Śvetodana,

78.s:
samūlaścaiva saralo ratnaketuśca parvataḥ .
ekamūlo mahāśrṛṅgo gajamūlo'pi śāvakaḥ .. 78.16 ..
78.d:
समूलश्चैव सरलो रत्नकेतुश्च पर्वतः ।
एकमूलो महाश्रृङ्गो गजमूलोऽपि शावकः ॥ 78.16 ॥
78.m: Samūla, Sarala, and the mountain Ratnaketu, / Ekamūla, Mahāśṛṅga, Gajamūla, and Śāvaka,

78.s:
pañcaśailaśca kailāso himavānacalottamaḥ .
uttarā ye mahāśailāstān vakṣyāmi nibodhata .. 78.17 ..
78.d:
पञ्चशैलश्च कैलासो हिमवानचलोत्तमः ।
उत्तरा ये महाशैलास्तान् वक्ष्यामि निबोधत ॥ 78.17 ॥
78.m: Pañcaśaila, Kailāsa, and Himavān, the best of mountains. / Now I shall declare the great northern mountains; learn of them:

78.s:
kapilaḥ piṅgalo bhadraḥ sarasaśca mahācalaḥ .
kumudo madhumāṃścaiva garjano markaṭastathā .. 78.18 ..
78.d:
कपिलः पिङ्गलो भद्रः सरसश्च महाचलः ।
कुमुदो मधुमांश्चैव गर्जनो मर्कटस्तथा ॥ 78.18 ॥
78.m: Kapila, Piṅgala, Bhadra, and the great mountain Sarasa, / Kumuda, Madhumān, Garjana, and Markaṭa,

78.s:
kṛṣṇaśca pāṇḍavaścaiva sahastraśirasastathā .
pāriyātraśca śailendraḥ śrṛṅgavānacalottamaḥ .
ityete parvatavarāḥ śrīmantaḥ paścime smṛtāḥ .. 78.19 ..
78.d:
कृष्णश्च पाण्डवश्चैव सहस्त्रशिरसस्तथा ।
पारियात्रश्च शैलेन्द्रः श्रृङ्गवानचलोत्तमः ।
इत्येते पर्वतवराः श्रीमन्तः पश्चिमे स्मृताः ॥ 78.19 ॥
78.m: Kṛṣṇa, Pāṇḍava, Sahasraśiras, / the king of mountains Pāriyātra, and Śṛṅgavān, the best of mountains— / these splendid ones are recorded as the foremost mountains in the west.

78.s:
mahābhadrasya sarasa uttareṇa dvijottamāḥ .
ye parvatāḥ sthitā viprāstān vakṣyāmi nibodhata .. 78.20 ..
78.d:
महाभद्रस्य सरस उत्तरेण द्विजोत्तमाः ।
ये पर्वताः स्थिता विप्रास्तान् वक्ष्यामि निबोधत ॥ 78.20 ॥
78.m: To the north of Lake Mahābhadra, O best of the twice-born, / O brāhmaṇas, are mountains situated there; I shall proclaim them; learn of them:

78.s:
haṃsakūṭo mahāśailo vṛṣahaṃsaśca parvataḥ .
kapiñjalaśca śailendra indraśailaśca sānumān .. 78.21 ..
78.d:
हंसकूटो महाशैलो वृषहंसश्च पर्वतः ।
कपिञ्जलश्च शैलेन्द्र इन्द्रशैलश्च सानुमान् ॥ 78.21 ॥
78.m: The great mountain Haṃsakūṭa, the mountain Vṛṣahaṃsa, / the king of mountains Kapiñjala, and the peaked Indraśaila,

78.s:
nīlaḥ kanakaśrṛṅgaśca śataśrṛṅgaśca parvataḥ .
puṣkaro meghaśailo'tha virajāścācalottamaḥ .
jāruciścaiva śailendra ityete uttarāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 78.22 ..
78.d:
नीलः कनकश्रृङ्गश्च शतश्रृङ्गश्च पर्वतः ।
पुष्करो मेघशैलोऽथ विरजाश्चाचलोत्तमः ।
जारुचिश्चैव शैलेन्द्र इत्येते उत्तराः स्मृताः ॥ 78.22 ॥
78.m: Nīla, Kanakaśṛṅga, the mountain Śataśṛṅga, / Puṣkara, then Meghaśaila, Virajas the best of mountains, / and the king of mountains Jāruci—these are recorded as the northern ones.

78.s:
ityeteṣāṃ tu mukhyānāmuttareṣu yathākramam .
sthalīrantaradroṇyaśca sarāṃsi ca nibodhata .. 78.23 ..
78.d:
इत्येतेषां तु मुख्यानामुत्तरेषु यथाक्रमम् ।
स्थलीरन्तरद्रोण्यश्च सरांसि च निबोधत ॥ 78.23 ॥
78.m: Now learn in proper order of the tablelands, / the intermediate valleys, and the lakes among these principal [mountains] in the north.

78.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre aṣṭasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 78 ..
78.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे अष्टसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 78 ॥
78.m: Thus ends the seventy-eighth chapter in the sacred scripture of the glorious Varāha Purāṇa.

79.s:
rudra uvāca .
sītāntasyācalendrasya kumudasyāntareṇa ca .
droṇyāṃ vihaṅgapuṣṭāyāṃ nānāsattvaniṣevitam .. 79.1 ..
79.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
सीतान्तस्याचलेन्द्रस्य कुमुदस्यान्तरेण च ।
द्रोण्यां विहङ्गपुष्टायां नानासत्त्वनिषेवितम् ॥ 79.1 ॥
79.m: Rudra said: / Between the king of mountains Sītānta and Kumuda, / in a valley nurtured with birds and frequented by diverse living beings,

79.s:
triyojanaśatāyāmaṃ śatayojanavistṛtam .
surasāmalapānīyaṃ ramyaṃ tatra surocanam .. 79.2 ..
79.d:
त्रियोजनशतायामं शतयोजनविस्तृतम् ।
सुरसामलपानीयं रम्यं तत्र सुरोचनम् ॥ 79.2 ॥
79.m: measuring three hundred yojanas in length and one hundred yojanas in width, / possessing delicious, clear water, lovely, and very radiant,

79.s:
droṇamātrapramāṇaiśca puṇḍarīkaiḥ sugandhibhiḥ .
sahastraśatapatraiśca mahāpadmairalaṅkṛtam .. 79.3 ..
79.d:
द्रोणमात्रप्रमाणैश्च पुण्डरीकैः सुगन्धिभिः ।
सहस्त्रशतपत्रैश्च महापद्मैरलङ्कृतम् ॥ 79.3 ॥
79.m: adorned with fragrant white lotuses measuring a droṇa in size, / and with great lotuses of a hundred thousand petals,

79.s:
devadānavagandharvairmahāsarpairadhiṣṭhitam .
puṇyaṃ tacchrīsaro nāma saprakāśamiheha ca .. 79.4 ..
79.d:
देवदानवगन्धर्वैर्महासर्पैरधिष्ठितम् ।
पुण्यं तच्छ्रीसरो नाम सप्रकाशमिहेह च ॥ 79.4 ॥
79.m: inhabited by gods, dānavas, gandharvas, and great serpents, / is that sacred [lake] named Śrīsaras, luminous here and there,

79.s:
prasannasalilaiḥ pūrṇaṃ śaraṇyaṃ sarvadehinām .
tatra tvekaṃ mahāpadmaṃ madhye padmavanasya ca .. 79.5 ..
79.d:
प्रसन्नसलिलैः पूर्णं शरण्यं सर्वदेहिनाम् ।
तत्र त्वेकं महापद्मं मध्ये पद्मवनस्य च ॥ 79.5 ॥
79.m: filled with serene waters, a refuge for all embodied beings. / There, in the middle of that forest of lotuses, is a single great lotus,

79.s:
koṭipatraprakalitaṃ taruṇādityavarcasam .
nityaṃ vyākośamadhuraṃ calatvādatimaṇḍalam .. 79.6 ..
79.d:
कोटिपत्रप्रकलितं तरुणादित्यवर्चसम् ।
नित्यं व्याकोशमधुरं चलत्वादतिमण्डलम् ॥ 79.6 ॥
79.m: composed of ten million petals, with the splendor of the rising sun, / ever fully blown, sweet, and perfectly circular as it sways,

79.s:
cārukesarajālāḍhyaṃ mattabhramaranāditam .
tasmin madhye bhagavatī sākṣāt śrīrnityameva hi .
lakṣmīstu taṃ tadāvāsaṃ mūrttimantaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 79.7 ..
79.d:
चारुकेसरजालाढ्यं मत्तभ्रमरनादितम् ।
तस्मिन् मध्ये भगवती साक्षात् श्रीर्नित्यमेव हि ।
लक्ष्मीस्तु तं तदावासं मूर्त्तिमन्तं न संशयः ॥ 79.7 ॥
79.m: rich with a beautiful mass of filaments, resounding with intoxicated bees. / In the middle of it is the goddess, Śrī herself, eternally; / Lakṣmī indeed has made that her embodied dwelling, without doubt.

79.s:
sarasastasya tīre tu tasmin siddhaniṣevitam .
sadā puṣpaphalaṃ ramyaṃ tatra bilvavanaṃ mahat .. 79.8 ..
79.d:
सरसस्तस्य तीरे तु तस्मिन् सिद्धनिषेवितम् ।
सदा पुष्पफलं रम्यं तत्र बिल्ववनं महत् ॥ 79.8 ॥
79.m: On the shore of that lake, frequented by the Siddhas, / there is a vast bilva forest, delightful, bearing flowers and fruit at all times,

79.s:
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ dviyojanaśatāyatam .
arddhakrośoccaśikharairmahāvṛkṣaiḥ samantataḥ .
śākhāsahastrakalitairmahāskandhaiḥ samākulam .. 79.9 ..
79.d:
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं द्वियोजनशतायतम् ।
अर्द्धक्रोशोच्चशिखरैर्महावृक्षैः समन्ततः ।
शाखासहस्त्रकलितैर्महास्कन्धैः समाकुलम् ॥ 79.9 ॥
79.m: one hundred yojanas wide and two hundred yojanas long, / crowded all around with huge trees whose peaks are half a krośa high, / having thousands of branches and enormous trunks,

79.s:
phalaiḥ sahastrasaṅkāśaiḥ haritaiḥ pāṇḍuraistathā .
amṛtasvādusadṛśairbherīmātraiḥ sugandhibhiḥ .. 79.10 ..
79.d:
फलैः सहस्त्रसङ्काशैः हरितैः पाण्डुरैस्तथा ।
अमृतस्वादुसदृशैर्भेरीमात्रैः सुगन्धिभिः ॥ 79.10 ॥
79.m: with thousands of fruits, green as well as pale yellow, / sweet-tasting like nectar, as large as kettledrums, and fragrant,

79.s:
śīryadbhiśca patadbhiśca kīrṇabhūmivanāntaram .
nāmnā tacchrīvanaṃ nāma sarvalokeṣu viśrutam .. 79.11 ..
79.d:
शीर्यद्भिश्च पतद्भिश्च कीर्णभूमिवनान्तरम् ।
नाम्ना तच्छ्रीवनं नाम सर्वलोकेषु विश्रुतम् ॥ 79.11 ॥
79.m: with the ground and the interior of the forest strewn with [fruits] falling and breaking apart. / By name, it is known throughout all the worlds as Śrīvana.

79.s:
devādibhiḥ samākīrṇamaṣṭābhiḥ kakubhiḥ śubham .
bilvāśibhiśca munibhiḥ sevitaṃ puṇyakāribhiḥ .
tatra śrīḥ saṃsthitā nityaṃ siddhasaṅghaniṣevitā .. 79.12 ..
79.d:
देवादिभिः समाकीर्णमष्टाभिः ककुभिः शुभम् ।
बिल्वाशिभिश्च मुनिभिः सेवितं पुण्यकारिभिः ।
तत्र श्रीः संस्थिता नित्यं सिद्धसङ्घनिषेविता ॥ 79.12 ॥
79.m: It is filled with gods and others, auspicious in all eight directions, / frequented by pious sages who subsist on bilva fruit. / There Śrī resides eternally, served by multitudes of Siddhas.

79.s:
ekaikasyācalendrasya maṇiśailasya cāntaram .
śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ dviyojanaśatāyatam .. 79.13 ..
79.d:
एकैकस्याचलेन्द्रस्य मणिशैलस्य चान्तरम् ।
शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं द्वियोजनशतायतम् ॥ 79.13 ॥
79.m: Between each single king of mountains and the Maṇi mountain, / extending one hundred yojanas in width and two hundred yojanas in length,

79.s:
vimalaṃ paṅkajavanaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam .
puṣpaṃ lakṣmyā dhṛtaṃ bhāti nityaṃ prajvalatīva ha .. 79.14 ..
79.d:
विमलं पङ्कजवनं सिद्धचारणसेवितम् ।
पुष्पं लक्ष्म्या धृतं भाति नित्यं प्रज्वलतीव ह ॥ 79.14 ॥
79.m: is a spotless forest of lotuses, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas. / The flower held by Lakṣmī shines, as if constantly blazing.

79.s:
arddhakrośaṃ ca śikharairmahāskandhaiḥ samāvṛtam .
praphullaśākhāśikharaṃ piñjaraṃ bhāti tadvanam .. 79.15 ..
79.d:
अर्द्धक्रोशं च शिखरैर्महास्कन्धैः समावृतम् ।
प्रफुल्लशाखाशिखरं पिञ्जरं भाति तद्वनम् ॥ 79.15 ॥
79.m: Surrounded by great trunks with summits half a krośa high, / with blossoming branches and crests, that forest appears golden-yellow,

79.s:
dvibāhupariṇāhaistaistrihastāyāmavistṛtaiḥ .
manaḥśilācūrṇanibhaiḥ pāṇḍukesaraśālibhiḥ .. 79.16 ..
79.d:
द्विबाहुपरिणाहैस्तैस्त्रिहस्तायामविस्तृतैः ।
मनःशिलाचूर्णनिभैः पाण्डुकेसरशालिभिः ॥ 79.16 ॥
79.m: pervaded by charming flowers that have the circumference of two arms / and are three hastas in length and width, / resembling powdered realgar, and possessing pale filaments,

79.s:
puṣpairmanoharairvyāptaṃ vyākośairgandhaśobhibhiḥ .
virājati vanaṃ sarvaṃ mattabhramaranāditam .. 79.17 ..
79.d:
पुष्पैर्मनोहरैर्व्याप्तं व्याकोशैर्गन्धशोभिभिः ।
विराजति वनं सर्वं मत्तभ्रमरनादितम् ॥ 79.17 ॥
79.m: fully blown and beautiful with fragrance. / The entire forest shines, resounding with intoxicated bees.

79.s:
tadvanaṃ dānavairdaityairgandharvairyakṣarākṣasaiḥ .
kinnarairapsarobhiśca mahābhogaiśca sevitam .. 79.18 ..
79.d:
तद्वनं दानवैर्दैत्यैर्गन्धर्वैर्यक्षराक्षसैः ।
किन्नरैरप्सरोभिश्च महाभोगैश्च सेवितम् ॥ 79.18 ॥
79.m: That forest is frequented by dānavas, daityas, gandharvas, yakṣas, and rākṣasas, / by kinnaras, apsarases, and great-hooded serpents.

79.s:
tatrāśramo bhagavataḥ kaśyapasya prajāpateḥ .
siddhasādhugaṇākīrṇaṃ nānāśramasamākulam .. 79.19 ..
79.d:
तत्राश्रमो भगवतः कश्यपस्य प्रजापतेः ।
सिद्धसाधुगणाकीर्णं नानाश्रमसमाकुलम् ॥ 79.19 ॥
79.m: There is the hermitage of the venerable Prajāpati Kaśyapa, / crowded with hosts of Siddhas and holy men, filled with various hermitages.

79.s:
mahānīlasya madhye tu kumbhasya ca girestathā .
madhye sukhā nadī nāma tasyāstīre mahadvanam .. 79.20 ..
79.d:
महानीलस्य मध्ये तु कुम्भस्य च गिरेस्तथा ।
मध्ये सुखा नदी नाम तस्यास्तीरे महद्वनम् ॥ 79.20 ॥
79.m: Between Mahānīla and the mountain Kumbha / is a river named Sukhā in the middle; on its bank is a vast forest,

79.s:
pañcāśadyojanāyāmaṃ triṃśadyojanamaṇḍalam .
ramyaṃ tālavanaṃ śrīmat krośārddhocchritapādapam .. 79.21 ..
79.d:
पञ्चाशद्योजनायामं त्रिंशद्योजनमण्डलम् ।
रम्यं तालवनं श्रीमत् क्रोशार्द्धोच्छ्रितपादपम् ॥ 79.21 ॥
79.m: fifty yojanas in length and thirty yojanas in circumference, / a charming, splendid palm grove whose trees rise half a krośa high,

79.s:
mahābalairmahāsāraiḥ sthirairavicalaiḥ śubhaiḥ .
mahadañjanasaṃsthānaiḥ parivṛttairmahāphalaiḥ .. 79.22 ..
79.d:
महाबलैर्महासारैः स्थिरैरविचलैः शुभैः ।
महदञ्जनसंस्थानैः परिवृत्तैर्महाफलैः ॥ 79.22 ॥
79.m: greatly strong, of high substance, firm, unmoving, and auspicious, / shaped like great collyrium-heaps, rounded, and with huge fruits,

79.s:
mṛṣṭagandhaguṇopetairupetaṃ siddhasevitam .
airāvatasya kariṇastatraiva samudāhṛtam .. 79.23 ..
79.d:
मृष्टगन्धगुणोपेतैरुपेतं सिद्धसेवितम् ।
ऐरावतस्य करिणस्तत्रैव समुदाहृतम् ॥ 79.23 ॥
79.m: endowed with pleasant scent and qualities, frequented by the Siddhas. / That very place is declared to belong to the elephant Airāvata.

79.s:
airāvatasya rudrasya devaśailasya cāntare .
sahastrayojanāyāmā śatayojanavistṛtā .. 79.24 ..
79.d:
ऐरावतस्य रुद्रस्य देवशैलस्य चान्तरे ।
सहस्त्रयोजनायामा शतयोजनविस्तृता ॥ 79.24 ॥
79.m: Between Airāvata, Rudra, and the mountain Devaśaila, / is [a region] a thousand yojanas long and a hundred yojanas wide,

79.s:
sarvā hyekaśilā bhūmirvṛkṣavīrudhavarjitā .
āplutā pādamātreṇa salilena samantataḥ .. 79.25 ..
79.d:
सर्वा ह्येकशिला भूमिर्वृक्षवीरुधवर्जिता ।
आप्लुता पादमात्रेण सलिलेन समन्ततः ॥ 79.25 ॥
79.m: where the ground is entirely a single sheet of rock, devoid of trees and creepers, / inundated all around with water merely a foot deep.

79.s:
ityetābhyantaradroṇyo nānākārāḥ prakīrttitāḥ .
meroḥ pārśvena viprendrā yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ .. 79.26 ..
79.d:
इत्येताभ्यन्तरद्रोण्यो नानाकाराः प्रकीर्त्तिताः ।
मेरोः पार्श्वेन विप्रेन्द्रा यथावदनुपूर्वशः ॥ 79.26 ॥
79.m: Thus these interior valleys of various forms / on the sides of Meru have been declared in proper order, O foremost of brāhmaṇas.

79.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre ekonāśītitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 79 ..
79.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे एकोनाशीतितमोऽध्यायः ॥ 79 ॥
79.m: Thus ends the seventy-ninth chapter in the sacred scripture of the glorious Varāha Purāṇa.

80.s:
rudra uvāca .
atha dakṣiṇadigvyavasthitāḥ parvatadroṇyaḥ siddhācaritāḥ
kīrtyante . śiśirapataṅgayormadhye śuklabhūmistriyā muktalatāgalitapādapam .
ikṣukṣepe ca śikhare pādapairupaśobhitam .
udumbaravanaṃ ramyaṃ pakṣisaṅghaniṣevitam .. 80.1 ..
phalitaṃ tad vanaṃ bhāti mahākūrmopamaiḥ phalaiḥ ..
tad vanaṃ devayonyo'ṣṭau sevante sarvadaiva .. 80.2 ..
tatra prasannasvādusalilā bahūdakā nadyo vahanti . tatrāśramo bhagavataḥ kardamasya prajāpateḥ . nānāmunijanākīrṇastacca śatayojanamekaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ vanaṃ ca .
tathā ca tāmrābhasya śailasya pataṅgasya cāntare śatayojanavistīrṇaṃ dviguṇāyataṃ bālārkasadṛśarājīvapuṇa़rīkaiḥ samantataḥ sahastrapatrairaviralairalaṃkṛtaṃ mahat saro'nekasiddhagandharvādhyuṣitam . .. 80.3 ..
tasya ca madhye mahāśikharaḥ śatayojanāyāmastriṃśadyojanavistīrṇo'nekadhāturatnabhūṣitastasya copari mahatī rathyā ratnaprākāratoraṇā .
tasyāṃ mahad vidyādharapuram . tatra pulomanāmā vidyādhararājaḥ śatasahastraparīvāraḥ .
tathā ca vikhākhācalendrasya śvetasya cāntare saraḥ .
tasya ca pūrvatīre mahadāmravanaṃ kanakasaṃkāśaiḥ phalairatisugandhibhirmahākumbhamātraiḥ sarvataścitam .
devagandharvādayaśca tatra nivasanti . ..4..
80.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
अथ दक्षिणदिग्व्यवस्थिताः पर्वतद्रोण्यः सिद्धाचरिताः
कीर्त्यन्ते । शिशिरपतङ्गयोर्मध्ये शुक्लभूमिस्त्रिया मुक्तलतागलितपादपम् ।
इक्षुक्षेपे च शिखरे पादपैरुपशोभितम् ।
उदुम्बरवनं रम्यं पक्षिसङ्घनिषेवितम् ॥ 80.1 ॥
फलितं तद् वनं भाति महाकूर्मोपमैः फलैः ॥
तद् वनं देवयोन्योऽष्टौ सेवन्ते सर्वदैव ॥ 80.2 ॥
तत्र प्रसन्नस्वादुसलिला बहूदका नद्यो वहन्ति । तत्राश्रमो भगवतः कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः । नानामुनिजनाकीर्णस्तच्च शतयोजनमेकं परिमण्डलं वनं च ।
तथा च ताम्राभस्य शैलस्य पतङ्गस्य चान्तरे शतयोजनविस्तीर्णं द्विगुणायतं बालार्कसदृशराजीवपुण़रीकैः समन्ततः सहस्त्रपत्रैरविरलैरलंकृतं महत् सरोऽनेकसिद्धगन्धर्वाध्युषितम् ॥। 80.3 ॥
तस्य च मध्ये महाशिखरः शतयोजनायामस्त्रिंशद्योजनविस्तीर्णोऽनेकधातुरत्नभूषितस्तस्य चोपरि महती रथ्या रत्नप्राकारतोरणा ।
तस्यां महद् विद्याधरपुरम् । तत्र पुलोमनामा विद्याधरराजः शतसहस्त्रपरीवारः ।
तथा च विखाखाचलेन्द्रस्य श्वेतस्य चान्तरे सरः ।
तस्य च पूर्वतीरे महदाम्रवनं कनकसंकाशैः फलैरतिसुगन्धिभिर्महाकुम्भमात्रैः सर्वतश्चितम् ।
देवगन्धर्वादयश्च तत्र निवसन्ति ॥.4॥
80.m:
Rudra said:
Now the mountain valleys situated in the southern direction, frequented by the Siddhas, are proclaimed: between Śiśira and Pataṅga is a white-ground land, with trees shedding dropped creepers, / adorned with trees on the peak at Ikṣukṣepa, / a lovely forest of udumbara trees frequented by flocks of birds;

that forest shines, laden with fruits resembling great tortoises; / the eight classes of divine beings always frequent that forest.

There rivers flow carrying abundant water, clear and sweet. There is the hermitage of Lord Kardama, the Prajāpati, crowded with various sages; and that forest is circular, one hundred yojanas [in extent]. / And likewise, between the copper-hued mountain and Pataṅga, there is a great lake inhabited by numerous Siddhas and Gandharvas, one hundred yojanas wide, twice as long, adorned all around with dense thousand-petaled lotuses and white water-lilies resembling the rising sun.

And in its middle is a great peak, one hundred yojanas in length and thirty yojanas in breadth, adorned with various minerals and gems; and above it is a great avenue endowed with ramparts and archways of gems. / On it is a great city of Vidyādharas. There lives the Vidyādhara king named Puloman, accompanied by a retinue of one hundred thousand. / And likewise, between Mount Viśākha and Śveta, there is a lake. / And on its eastern bank is a great mango forest, covered all over with fruits resembling gold, extremely fragrant, each the size of a large water-jar. / And gods, Gandharvas, and others dwell there.
Between the king of mountains Sumula and Mount Vasudhāra, measuring thirty yojanas in width and fifty yojanas in length,

80.s:
bilvasthalī nāma . tatra phalāni vidrumasaṃkāśāni taiśca patadbhiḥ sthalamṛttikā klinnā . tāṃ ca sthalīṃ suguhyakādayaḥ sevante bilvaphalāśinaḥ .
tathā ca vasudhāraratnadhārayorantare triṃśadyojanavistīrṇaṃ śatayojanamāyataṃ sugandhikiṃśukavanaṃ sadākusumaṃ yasya gandhena vāsyate yojanaśatam .
tatra siddhādhyuṣitaṃ jalopetaṃ ca . ..6..
80.d:
बिल्वस्थली नाम । तत्र फलानि विद्रुमसंकाशानि तैश्च पतद्भिः स्थलमृत्तिका क्लिन्ना । तां च स्थलीं सुगुह्यकादयः सेवन्ते बिल्वफलाशिनः ।
तथा च वसुधाररत्नधारयोरन्तरे त्रिंशद्योजनविस्तीर्णं शतयोजनमायतं सुगन्धिकिंशुकवनं सदाकुसुमं यस्य गन्धेन वास्यते योजनशतम् ।
तत्र सिद्धाध्युषितं जलोपेतं च ॥.6॥
80.m: is [a plateau] named Bilvasthalī. There the fruits resemble coral, and the soil of the plateau is moistened by them as they fall. Frequented by noble Guhyakas and others, who feed on bilva fruits, is that plateau. / And between Mount Vasudhāra and Mount Ratnadhāra there is a fragrant kiṃśuka grove, thirty yojanas wide and one hundred yojanas long, always in blossom, whose fragrance perfumes an area of a hundred yojanas. / It is inhabited by Siddhas and endowed with water.

80.s:
tatra cādityasya devasya mahadāyatanam .
samāse māse ca bhagavānavatarati sūryaḥ prajāpatiḥ .
kālajanakaṃ devādayo namasyanti .
tathā ca pañcakūṭasya kailāsasya cāntare sahastrayojanāyāmaṃ vistīrṇaṃ śatayojanaṃ haṃsapāṇḍuraṃ kṣudrasattvairanādhṛṣyaṃ svargasopānamiva bhūmaṇḍalam . ..7..
80.d:
तत्र चादित्यस्य देवस्य महदायतनम् ।
समासे मासे च भगवानवतरति सूर्यः प्रजापतिः ।
कालजनकं देवादयो नमस्यन्ति ।
तथा च पञ्चकूटस्य कैलासस्य चान्तरे सहस्त्रयोजनायामं विस्तीर्णं शतयोजनं हंसपाण्डुरं क्षुद्रसत्त्वैरनाधृष्यं स्वर्गसोपानमिव भूमण्डलम् ॥.7॥
80.m: And there is a great temple of the sun-god, Āditya. / Month after month, the Lord Prajāpati Sūrya descends [there]. / Gods and others pay homage to him, the producer of time. / And between Pañcakūṭa and Kailāsa there is a region of the earth, one thousand yojanas long and one hundred yojanas wide, white as a swan, unapproachable by base creatures, resembling a stairway to heaven.

80.s:
atha paścimadigbhāge vyavasthitā giridroṇyaḥ kīrtyante . supārśvaśikhiśailayormadhye samantād yojanaśatamekaṃ bhaumaśilātalaṃ nityataptaṃ duḥsparśam .
tasya madhye triṃśadyojanavistīrṇaṃ maṇḍalaṃ vahnisthānam . sa ca sarvakālamanindhano bhagavān lokakṣayakārī saṃvartako jvalate .
antare ca śailavarayoḥ kumudāñjanayoḥ śatayojanavistīrṇāmātuluṅgasthalī sarvasattvānāmagamyā . pītavarṇaiḥ phalairāvṛtā satī sā sthalī śobhate .
tatra ca puṇyo hradaḥ siddhairupetaḥ. bṛhaspatestadvanam.. tathā ca śailayoḥ piñjaragaurayorantareṇa sarodroṇī hyanekaśatayojanāyatā mahadbhiśca ṣaṭpadodghuṣṭaiḥ kumudairupaśobhitā . ..8..
80.d:
अथ पश्चिमदिग्भागे व्यवस्थिता गिरिद्रोण्यः कीर्त्यन्ते । सुपार्श्वशिखिशैलयोर्मध्ये समन्ताद् योजनशतमेकं भौमशिलातलं नित्यतप्तं दुःस्पर्शम् ।
तस्य मध्ये त्रिंशद्योजनविस्तीर्णं मण्डलं वह्निस्थानम् । स च सर्वकालमनिन्धनो भगवान् लोकक्षयकारी संवर्तको ज्वलते ।
अन्तरे च शैलवरयोः कुमुदाञ्जनयोः शतयोजनविस्तीर्णामातुलुङ्गस्थली सर्वसत्त्वानामगम्या । पीतवर्णैः फलैरावृता सती सा स्थली शोभते ।
तत्र च पुण्यो ह्रदः सिद्धैरुपेतः। बृहस्पतेस्तद्वनम्॥ तथा च शैलयोः पिञ्जरगौरयोरन्तरेण सरोद्रोणी ह्यनेकशतयोजनायता महद्भिश्च षट्पदोद्घुष्टैः कुमुदैरुपशोभिता ॥.8॥
80.m:
Now the mountain valleys situated in the western direction are described:
Between the mountains Supārśva and Śikhi, for one hundred yojanas all around, there is a flat rocky ground, constantly burning and hard to touch. / In its center is an area thirty yojanas wide, the place of fire. And at all times, without fuel, the venerable Saṃvartaka, who destroys the worlds, blazes there. / And between the two excellent mountains Kumuda and Añjana is a plateau of citron trees, one hundred yojanas wide, impassable to all living beings. Covered with yellow fruits, that plateau shines. / And there is a sacred pool frequented by Siddhas. That grove belongs to Bṛhaspati. And between the two mountains Piñjara and Gaura is a lake valley, many hundreds of yojanas long, adorned with large white water-lilies resounded by bees.

80.s:
tatra ca bhagavato viṣṇoḥ parameśvarasyāyatanam .
tathā ca śuklapāṇḍurayorapi mahāgiryorantare triṃśadyojanavistīrṇo navatyāyata ekaḥ śiloddeśovṛkṣavivarjitaḥ . tatra niṣpaṅkā dīrghikā savṛkṣā ca sthalapadminī anekajātīyaiśca padmaiḥ śobhitā .
tasyāśca madhye pañcayojanapramāṇo mahānyagrodhavṛkṣaḥ . tasmiṃścandraśekharomāpatirnīlavāsāśca devo nivasati yakṣādibhirīḍyamānaḥ .
sahastraśikharasya gireḥ kumudasya cāntare pañcāśadyojanāyāmaṃ viṃśadyojanavistṛtamikṣukṣepoccaśikharamanekapakṣisevitam .
anekavṛkṣaphalairmadhurastravairupaśobhitam .
tatra cendrasya mahānāśramo divyābhiprāyanirmitaḥ .
tathā ca śaṅkhakūṭaṛṣabhayormadhye puruṣasthalīramyā'nekaguṇānekayojanāyatā bilvapramāṇaiḥ kaṅkolakaiḥ sugandhibhirupetā .
tatra puruṣakarasonmattā nāgādyāḥ prativasanti . ..9..
80.d:
तत्र च भगवतो विष्णोः परमेश्वरस्यायतनम् ।
तथा च शुक्लपाण्डुरयोरपि महागिर्योरन्तरे त्रिंशद्योजनविस्तीर्णो नवत्यायत एकः शिलोद्देशोवृक्षविवर्जितः । तत्र निष्पङ्का दीर्घिका सवृक्षा च स्थलपद्मिनी अनेकजातीयैश्च पद्मैः शोभिता ।
तस्याश्च मध्ये पञ्चयोजनप्रमाणो महान्यग्रोधवृक्षः । तस्मिंश्चन्द्रशेखरोमापतिर्नीलवासाश्च देवो निवसति यक्षादिभिरीड्यमानः ।
सहस्त्रशिखरस्य गिरेः कुमुदस्य चान्तरे पञ्चाशद्योजनायामं विंशद्योजनविस्तृतमिक्षुक्षेपोच्चशिखरमनेकपक्षिसेवितम् ।
अनेकवृक्षफलैर्मधुरस्त्रवैरुपशोभितम् ।
तत्र चेन्द्रस्य महानाश्रमो दिव्याभिप्रायनिर्मितः ।
तथा च शङ्खकूटऋषभयोर्मध्ये पुरुषस्थलीरम्याऽनेकगुणानेकयोजनायता बिल्वप्रमाणैः कङ्कोलकैः सुगन्धिभिरुपेता ।
तत्र पुरुषकरसोन्मत्ता नागाद्याः प्रतिवसन्ति ॥.9॥
80.m: And there is a temple of the Lord Viṣṇu, the supreme master. / And between the two great mountains Śukla and Pāṇḍura is a certain rocky plateau, thirty yojanas wide and ninety long, devoid of trees. There is a mud-free pool with trees and a land-lotus garden adorned with various kinds of lotuses. / In its center is a great banyan tree measuring five yojanas. In it dwells the blue-robed god, the husband of Umā, who bears the crescent moon on his crest, praised by Yakṣas and others. / Between Mount Sahastraśikhara and Mount Kumuda is a [valley] fifty yojanas long and twenty yojanas wide, with a high peak reaching the height of a sugarcane's throw, frequented by many birds, / and adorned with fruits of various trees exuding sweetness. / There is Indra's great hermitage, built according to divine design. / And between Śaṅkhakūṭa and Ṛṣabha is the delightful Puruṣasthalī, extending many yojanas in various ways, endowed with fragrant kaṅkola fruits the size of bilva fruits. / There Nāgas and others, intoxicated by the juice of the puruṣaka, dwell.

80.s:
tathā kapiñjalanāgaśailayorantare dviśatayojanamāyāmavistīrṇā śatayojanasthalī nānāvanavibhūṣitā drākṣākharjūrakhaṇḍairupetā anekavṛkṣavallībhiranekaiśca sarobhirupetā sā sthalī .
tathā ca puṣkaramahāmeghayorantare ṣaṣṭiyojanavistīrṇā śatāyāmā pāṇitalaprakhyā mahatī sthalī vṛkṣavīrudhavivarjitā .tasyāśca pārśve catvāri mahāvanāni sarāṃsi cānekayojanānām .daśa pañca sapta tathāṣṭau triṃśad viṃśati yojanānāṃ sthalyo droṇyaśca . tatra kāścinmahāghorāḥ parvatakṣayāḥ . ..10..
80.d:
तथा कपिञ्जलनागशैलयोरन्तरे द्विशतयोजनमायामविस्तीर्णा शतयोजनस्थली नानावनविभूषिता द्राक्षाखर्जूरखण्डैरुपेता अनेकवृक्षवल्लीभिरनेकैश्च सरोभिरुपेता सा स्थली ।
तथा च पुष्करमहामेघयोरन्तरे षष्टियोजनविस्तीर्णा शतायामा पाणितलप्रख्या महती स्थली वृक्षवीरुधविवर्जिता ।तस्याश्च पार्श्वे चत्वारि महावनानि सरांसि चानेकयोजनानाम् ।दश पञ्च सप्त तथाष्टौ त्रिंशद् विंशति योजनानां स्थल्यो द्रोण्यश्च । तत्र काश्चिन्महाघोराः पर्वतक्षयाः ॥.10॥
80.m: And between the mountains Kapiñjala and Nāgaśaila is a plateau, two hundred yojanas long and one hundred yojanas wide, adorned with various groves, provided with tracts of grapes and dates, and endowed with many trees, vines, and numerous lakes. / And between Puṣkara and Mahāmegha is a vast plateau, sixty yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long, smooth as the palm of a hand, devoid of trees and shrubs. On its border are four great groves and lakes extending many yojanas. There are plateaus and valleys of ten, five, seven, eight, thirty, and twenty yojanas. There are certain mountain recesses that are exceedingly terrifying.
Thus ends the eightieth chapter in the venerable Varāha Purāṇa, a sacred scripture of the Lord.

81.s:
rudra uvāca .
ataḥ paraṃ parvateṣu devānāmavakāśā varṇyante .
tatra yo'sau śāntākhyaḥ parvatastasyopari mahendrasya krīḍāsthānam .
tatra devarājasya pārijātakavṛkṣavanam .
tasya pūrvapārśve kuñjaro nāma giriḥ .
tasyopari dānavānāmaṣṭau purāṇi ca . 1
81.d:
रुद्र उवाच ।
अतः परं पर्वतेषु देवानामवकाशा वर्ण्यन्ते ।
तत्र योऽसौ शान्ताख्यः पर्वतस्तस्योपरि महेन्द्रस्य क्रीडास्थानम् ।
तत्र देवराजस्य पारिजातकवृक्षवनम् ।
तस्य पूर्वपार्श्वे कुञ्जरो नाम गिरिः ।
तस्योपरि दानवानामष्टौ पुराणि च । 1
81.m:
Rudra said:
Hereafter, the dwelling-places of the gods on the mountains are described:
There, on the mountain called Śānta, is the pleasure ground of Mahendra. / There is the grove of pārijāta trees belonging to the king of the gods. / On its eastern flank is a mountain named Kuñjara. / Upon it are eight cities of the Dānavas.

81.s:
tathā vajrake parvatavare rākṣasānāmanekāni purāṇi .
te ca nāmnā nīlakāḥ kāmarūpiṇaḥ .
mahānīle'pi śailendrapurāṇi .
pañcadaśasahastrāṇi kinnarāṇāṃ khyātāni .
tatra devadattacandrādayo rājānaḥ .
pañcadaśakinnarāṇāṃ garvitāḥ .
tāni sauvarṇāni bilapraveśanāni ca purāṇi .
candrodaye ca parvatavare nāgānāmadhivāsaḥ .
te ca bilapraveśāḥ bileṣu vainateyaviṣayāvarttino vyavasthitānurāge ca dānavendrā vyavasthitāḥ .
veṇumatyapi vidyādharapuratrayaṃ .
triṃśadyojanaśatavistīrṇamekaikaṃ tāvadāyatam .
ulūkaromaśamahāvetrādayaśca rājāno vidyādharāṇām . 2
81.d:
तथा वज्रके पर्वतवरे राक्षसानामनेकानि पुराणि ।
ते च नाम्ना नीलकाः कामरूपिणः ।
महानीलेऽपि शैलेन्द्रपुराणि ।
पञ्चदशसहस्त्राणि किन्नराणां ख्यातानि ।
तत्र देवदत्तचन्द्रादयो राजानः ।
पञ्चदशकिन्नराणां गर्विताः ।
तानि सौवर्णानि बिलप्रवेशनानि च पुराणि ।
चन्द्रोदये च पर्वतवरे नागानामधिवासः ।
ते च बिलप्रवेशाः बिलेषु वैनतेयविषयावर्त्तिनो व्यवस्थितानुरागे च दानवेन्द्रा व्यवस्थिताः ।
वेणुमत्यपि विद्याधरपुरत्रयं ।
त्रिंशद्योजनशतविस्तीर्णमेकैकं तावदायतम् ।
उलूकरोमशमहावेत्रादयश्च राजानो विद्याधराणाम् । 2
81.m:
Likewise, on the excellent mountain Vajraka, there are many cities of the rākṣasas.
They are named Nīlakas, shape-shifters.
On Mahānīla also are the cities of the king of mountains.
Fifteen thousand are famed as those of the kinnaras.
There kings such as Devadatta and Candra [reside],
proud among the fifteen [classes of] kinnaras.
Those cities are made of gold and enter into caves.
And on the excellent mountain Candrodaya is the abode of the nāgas.
They enter caves; in the caves, situated in the realm of Garuḍa, and in [a place of] settled affection, the lords of dānavas abide.
On Veṇumant as well is a triad of cities of the vidyādharas,
each thirty leagues wide and just as long.
And kings of the vidyādharas, such as Ulūkaroman and Mahāvetra, [rule there].

81.s:
ekaike ca śailarājani svayameva garuḍo vyavasthitaḥ .
kuñjare tu parvatavare nityaṃ paśupatiḥ sthitaḥ .
